title: Lauren Daigle Has Released Christmas Music, So the Holiday Season Is Officially Open
summary: Every November, somewhere in a secure facility, a team of professionals gently thaws Mariah Carey so she can sing “All I Want for Christmas Is You” for the entire planet. Christian music has its own version of this tradition, and her name is Lauren Daigle. While nobody has to thaw her—she’s been out here the whole…
summary_zh: 每年11月，在一个安全设施的某个地方，一个专业团队会温柔地解冻Mariah Carey ，这样她就可以为整个星球唱“All I Want for Christmas Is You”。基督教音乐有自己的传统，她的名字叫劳伦·戴格尔（ Lauren Daigle ）。虽然没有人需要解冻她，但她一直在这里……
title_zh: Lauren Daigle发布圣诞音乐，圣诞季正式开放
content: Every November, somewhere in a secure facility, a team of professionals gently thaws Mariah Carey so she can sing “All I Want for Christmas Is You” for the entire planet. Christian music has its own version of this tradition, and her name is Lauren Daigle. While nobody has to thaw her—she’s been out here the whole time—this weekend she released two more holiday songs, this time with the Preservation Hall Jazz Band: “Sleigh Ride” and “Go Tell It on the Mountain.” If you feel like it is too early for this, please know that the paperwork has been filed. Halloween is over, the candy has been marked down to 50 percent, and the Christmas music season has legally begun. For anyone keeping score at home, this is not a new hobby for her. Daigle’s first Christmas album, Behold , came out in 2016 and climbed to No. 29 on the Billboard 200. It also started a tradition: the Behold Christmas Tour, which returns this December for its 10th annual run. That is the real Mariah comparison. A holiday arrives, and so does Lauren Daigle, with a setlist and a very good coat. The new songs are a pair of old favorites with a New Orleans accent. “Sleigh Ride” is the one that has been running through department stores since before you were born, and “Go Tell It on the Mountain” is the spiritual that has been spreading the Good News even longer than that. Preservation Hall brings the brass, the swing, and the general feeling that a very good party has broken out in a church basement. They also joined her last December for a holiday medley at the CMA Country Christmas special, so the chemistry was already on the record. There is also a business angle, if you like those. It is her first release on Capitol, Interscope and CCMG, which is a lot of letters to put on one sleigh. The songs will come out on a 7-inch vinyl on Nov. 27, the day after Thanksgiving, so you can be a person who owns a Christmas record while also being a person who is still full of pie. And if recorded music is not enough, the 10th annual Behold Christmas Tour opens Dec. 2 at the Ryman in Nashville, with stops in New Orleans and Orlando to follow. It is a beautiful room that was built for exactly this kind of evening, and it will probably smell like cinnamon candles and good intentions. The thaw has happened, the songs are out, and the season has officially been declared open. Please enjoy your holidays responsibly, which in this case means having “Sleigh Ride” on rotation.
content_zh:
每年11月,在一个安全的设施里,一群专业人士轻轻地解冻了Mariah Carey,这样她就能为整个地球唱出“我渴望的只有你”。 基督教音乐有它自己的这种传统版本,她叫劳伦·戴格.

这个周末她又发行了两首节日歌曲, 如果你觉得现在为时尚早,请知道文件已经归档。

万圣节结束,糖果被标记为50%,圣诞音乐季合法开始. 对于任何在家记分的人来说,这不是她的新爱好. Daigle的首张圣诞专辑"Beye"于2016年出道并登上"Billboard 200"的29号. 它也开创了传统: 圣诞之旅,

这是真正的Mariah比较。 节日到来 Lauren Daigle也来了 里面有固定名单 外衣很好看 新歌是一对有"新奥尔良口音"的旧相声. " 雪橇骑 " 是自你出生前就一直在百货公司跑来跑去的一款,而 " 在山上说吧 " 是传播 " 好消息 " 的时间甚至更长的精神。

保存 霍尔带来了青铜器,秋千,以及一般感觉一个非常好的聚会在教堂地下室爆发了. 他们去年12月也加入她,参加CMA乡村圣诞特辑会的节日梅德利会,因此化学已经录制了. 也有一个商业角度,如果你喜欢这些。

这是她首次在Capitol,Interscope和CCMG上发布,这是许多要放上雪橇的信. 歌曲会在感恩节后第二天的11月27日以7英寸的花花筒出道,这样你就可以成为拥有圣诞唱片的人,同时也是仍然充满了派的人. 如果录制的音乐还不够的话,第10届年度"看圣诞之旅"(Book Christmas Tour)将于12月开通.

2个在纳什维尔的雷曼车站,在新奥尔良和奥兰多停站后再跟进. 这是一个美丽的房间, 建造的正是这种夜晚, 它可能闻起来像肉桂蜡烛和良好意图。 冰冻已出,歌曲已出道,赛季正式宣布开播.

请以负责任的方式享受假期,这意味着轮回“雪橇骑”。
author: RELEVANT Staff

title: Inside Indie Tribe’s Plan to Disrupt Christian Hip-Hop
summary: On 'Who Do You Say I Am?', the Christian hip-hop collective reads the Bible's villains with empathy — and asks the church to do the same for everyone it writes off.
summary_zh: 在《你说我是谁？》（ Who Do You Say I Am? ）一文中，这位基督教嘻哈乐队以同理心解读了《圣经》中的恶棍，并要求教会为它所注销的每一个人做同样的事情。
title_zh: 探索独立部落颠覆基督教嘻哈的计划
content: Somewhere in the middle of talking about Scripture, Indie Tribe starts arguing about how to describe someone getting kicked in the groin. nobigdyl., Jon Keith, Mogli the Iceburg and DJ Mykael V are mid-sentence about the theological weight of community when the conversation collapses into a bit about their bandmate, Torey D’Shaun, who has stepped out and, per group tradition, is simply “in the bathroom.” The jokes runs a full minute before anyone remembers what they were talking about. This is more or less Indie Tribe’s operating system: theology, friendship, music and dumb jokes occupying the same room. Their new album, Who Do You Say I Am? , works the same way. They didn’t set out to make a concept record. nobigdyl., Jon Keith, Mogli and Mykael V have been a unit for years, joined more recently by D’Shaun, who folded into the group in 2024 in the middle of an album cycle. Their process has never looked like a studio session. It looks like a household. “We live together and eat together, pray together, we do Bible studies, all that kind of stuff, and we make music for a week,” Jon Keith says. They don’t start with a concept. They start with proximity, then look back at what they made and find the thread already running through it. “We kind of look at the range of the songs that we’re making,” Jon Keith says. “We’re like, ‘Okay, it kind of feels like God is moving this in a certain direction.’” Who Do You Say I Am? happened that way. Written and recorded in December 2024 and released March 27 this year, it’s the first project to feature D’Shaun from the ground up, and the group says his arrival changed the chemistry entirely. “This is really the first time to me that it feels like — I love our previous albums, but the way that this album has a heart and a story to it and a concept, it makes the other albums feel like mixtapes,” Jon Keith says. “This joint is easily the longest album we’ve done. It really feels like our first album album.” The title eventually gave them the question holding the record together: What does it actually feel like to be the person history remembers as the villain? “It’s the product of a lot of introspection that we’ve had,” Mogli says. “We’ve gone through the Bible together multiple times through different lenses, at different times in life when we’re going through different things.” The goal wasn’t to defend bad behavior. It was to stop flattening biblical figures into cautionary tales and start reading them like people, asking how it feels to be the character everyone’s quick to condemn. nobigdyl. pushes it further. The discomfort people feel toward Scripture’s messier figures, he argues, says more about a failure of imagination than a failure of faith. Take David, a man the Bible treats as a hero despite a life that would read as chaos by modern standards. “If you take David’s context and put it now, he sounds like Future,” nobigdyl. says. “How many baby moms he got? OK, you’re Nick Cannon.” The Bible’s heroes, he says, were “tripping the same way” as the people society is quick to write off today. For Keith, that cuts both directions. Indie Tribe wants listeners to extend the same grace to people outside the church that Christians are often quick to withhold. “We want to be disruptive to the world, but we also want to be disruptive to the church,” he says. “We want to wake them up.” He points to how easily Christians distance themselves from people whose lives look nothing like the ones they consider acceptable. “They’re still made in the image of God, and God is still able to work on these people,” he says. “The only thing that’s going to get you sent to hell is not belonging to Jesus. That’s it.” It’s a theology built for people who’ve already decided church isn’t for them, people nobigdyl. describes as not being “super theological” or part of “the Christian culture.” The album’s central question, borrowed from the moment Jesus asks his disciples who they say he is, is an invitation the group

title: This Sunday, the Global Church Will Pray for 388 Million Christians Facing High Levels of Persecution
summary: Congregations around the world will set aside Sunday, Nov. 1 for the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church, and this year Open Doors, the Christian ministry that tracks persecution, is asking them to start with Syria. Its 2026 World Watch List moved Syria from 18th place to sixth, a 12-point jump in its…
summary_zh: 世界各地的会众将于11月1日星期日为受迫害教会的国际祈祷日腾出时间，今年，追踪迫害的基督教事工敞开大门，要求他们从叙利亚开始。其2026年《世界观察榜》将叙利亚从第18位提升至第6位，其…
title_zh: 本周日，全球教会将为面临严重迫害的3.88亿基督徒祈祷
content: Congregations around the world will set aside Sunday, Nov. 1 for the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church, and this year Open Doors, the Christian ministry that tracks persecution, is asking them to start with Syria. Its 2026 World Watch List moved Syria from 18th place to sixth, a 12-point jump in its score and the largest in the top 10. Open Doors says Syria is now at its most dangerous for Christians since the Islamic State group occupied significant parts of the country. About 300,000 Christians live in Syria. Since the fall of the Assad government in December 2024, the country has been mostly controlled by forces led by Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham, an Islamic extremist group with roots in al-Qaeda. The group has made overtures toward moderation and held talks with representatives of Syria’s traditional Christian communities, but it is too soon to know what will come of the new leadership. Widespread instability has produced deadly clashes that have affected Druze and Alawites in particular, with Christians caught in the crossfire, and Islamic State attacks have resumed, including the deadly attack on a church in Damascus in June 2025. “The trauma of what happened hit us all hard,” said “Mourad,” who is responsible for the work of Open Doors’ local partner in Syria. “We thought getting rid of the previous regime would give us some sense of freedom, yet it seems there are still people who only believe in killing.” The interim Syrian constitution adopted in March 2025 makes Islamic law the main source of legislation, and it offers insufficient protection for religious minorities. Pressure on Christians is greatest in Damascus and Aleppo, while the northeast is generally safer. The World Watch List ranks the 50 countries where Christians face the most extreme persecution, using a points system built on data from experts on the ground in 100 countries. North Korea is first with a score of 97 out of 100, followed by Somalia, Yemen, Sudan and Eritrea. Syria is sixth with 90, ahead of Nigeria, Pakistan, Libya and Iran. Open Doors counts more than 388 million Christians worldwide facing high levels of persecution and discrimination for their faith, about one in seven, and in the top 50 countries alone, more than 315 million face very high or extreme persecution. In its 2026 report it recorded 4,849 Christians killed, 4,712 detained and 3,632 churches and Christian properties attacked. For more than 1,600 years Christians have set aside early November to remember believers who suffered for their faith. Open Doors’ free toolkit for churches and small groups includes guided prayer points, videos, sermon material and social images, and this year’s focus is the Middle East, beginning with Syria. Open Doors’ prayer points for Syria ask for three things: that believers would lean on God as their “Rock eternal” (Isaiah 26:4), that converts from Islam would find love and fellowship even when family and friends reject them, and that the victims of the Damascus church attack would feel God’s closeness.
content_zh: 世界范围内的教会将预留11月1日为受迫害教会国际祈祷日, 今年追踪迫害的基督教部也要求他们从叙利亚开始。 其2026年世界观察榜将叙利亚从第18名提升到第6名,比分跳出12分,位列前10名. 叙利亚现在对基督徒来说是最危险的, 约30万基督徒居住在叙利亚. 自2024年12月阿萨德政府倒台后,该国多由伊斯兰极端主义团体"基地"(Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham)所领导的势力所控制. 这个团体向着温和的态度,并与叙利亚传统基督教社区的代表举行了会谈,但现在还不知道新领导人会怎样。 普遍的不稳定导致了致命的冲突,尤其影响到德鲁兹人和阿拉维人,基督徒陷入了交火中,伊斯兰国又恢复了袭击,包括2025年6月大马士革一教堂被致命袭击. Mourad对叙利亚当地合作伙伴的工作负责。 “我们认为摆脱前政权会给我们一些自由感, 2025年3月通过的叙利亚临时宪法将伊斯兰法作为立法的主要来源,对宗教少数群体的保护不足. 大马士革和阿勒颇对基督徒的压力最大,而东北部一般比较安全. 世界观察列表将基督徒面临最极端迫害的50个国家排行榜,使用基于100个国家当地专家数据建立的分数系统. 朝鲜以97胜100负的分数排名第一,其次是索马里,也门,苏丹和厄立特里亚. 叙利亚以90分位列第六,领先尼日利亚,巴基斯坦,利比亚和伊朗. 开放门人数超过3.88亿,全世界因信仰而面临严重迫害和歧视的基督教徒约有七分之一,仅在前50个国家,就有3.15亿多基督教徒面临极高或极端迫害。 它在2026年的报告中记录了4 849名基督徒被杀死,4 712人被拘押,3 632所教堂和基督教财产被袭击。 1600多年以来,基督徒在11月上旬留作纪念因信仰而受苦受难的信徒. 开放的门对教堂和小团体免费的工具包包括导游的祈祷要点、录像、布道材料和社会形象,今年的重点是中东,首先是叙利亚。 开放的门对叙利亚的祈祷点要求三件事:信徒们倚靠上帝作为他们的"永生"(Isaiah 26:4),从伊斯兰教皈依的人即使家人和朋友拒绝也会找到爱和友谊,大马士革教堂袭击的受害者也会感受到上帝的亲切.
author: RELEVANT Staff

summary: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham told Theo Von on his podcast that nothing a person does or doesn’t do can separate them from God’s love, after Von said he wishes his connection with God were stronger. The conversation is in episode No. 692 of This Past Weekend. Von said his prayer connection with God is…
summary_zh: 印第安纳热病后卫索菲·坎宁安（ Sophie Cunningham ）在播客中告诉西奥·冯（ Theo Von ） ，在冯（ Von ）说他希望自己与上帝的联系更加紧密之后，一个人所做或不做的任何事情都不能将他们与上帝的爱分开。谈话发生在《This Past Weekend》第692期。冯说，他与上帝的祈祷联系是……
title_zh: WNBA明星索菲·坎宁安（ Sophie Cunningham ）致西奥·冯（ Theo Von ） ： “你所做的一切都不会让你与上帝的爱、恩典和宽恕分开”
content: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham told Theo Von on his podcast that nothing a person does or doesn’t do can separate them from God’s love, after Von said he wishes his connection with God were stronger. The conversation is in episode No. 692 of This Past Weekend . Von said his prayer connection with God is the part of his life he likes most, but that when he gets too busy it can feel disconnected. “I wish my connection was stronger,” he said. Cunningham answered, “Dude, I feel you,” and said she was saying it for other people listening too: “There’s nothing that you can or can’t do that’s going to separate you from God’s love and grace and forgiveness. Like that’s why Jesus came and died on the cross because he already knew everything you were going to do.” She added that what comes next is up to the person, who can “educate yourself and read the Bible,” but that “you’re already forgiven.” She also said she feels most connected when she is “prayed up,” a phrase Von said he likes and hears from a friend all the time. Earlier in the conversation, Cunningham said she relies on her faith because of what she does for a living. “You get a lot of hate, you get a lot of praise,” she said. Faith keeps her stable and “who I am,” she said, and she doesn’t care what people’s opinions are about her “because I’m not living for their praise.” Von later asked whether the media is unfair to Christians. Cunningham said that depends on perspective, but that she loves seeing more people say they are believers. “I feel like there’s a revival happening,” she said. She said it can be scary to speak up because people have had bad experiences with church, and that she likes seeing athletes with big platforms be “bold and courageous and come out about Jesus.” Von said more athletes he has gotten to know in the past four years seem to have faith, and that more of his friends are trying to learn about it too. “We want to have some more religious figures on to talk about stuff on here,” he said.
content_zh: 印地安那州狂热卫士苏菲·坎宁安(Sophie Cunningham)在播客上告诉西奥·冯(Theo Von)说,任何人做或不做都不能将他们与上帝的爱分开,因为冯说他希望他与上帝的联系更紧密。 对话在"过去的周末"第692集里进行。 冯说,他与上帝的祷告联系是他最喜欢的人生的一部分,但是当他忙到太忙时,会感到脱节. 他说,“我希望我的联系更加紧密。” 坎宁安回答说,“兄弟,我感觉到了,”她说,“你对别人也说,“你无法或不能做任何事情,都会把你与上帝的爱、恩惠和宽恕分开。 因为耶稣已经知道你们将要做的事, 她补充说,接下来要由一个人来决定,他可以“教育自己并阅读圣经 ” , 但“你已经被原谅了 ” 。 她还说,当她“振作起来”时,她感到联系最紧密。 冯说,他一直喜欢和听到一个朋友的话。 在谈话的早些时候,坎宁安说,由于她从事的工作,她依靠自己的信仰. 她说,“你得到许多仇恨,你得到许多赞美。” 她并不关心人们对她的看法, “因为我不为他们的赞美而活。” 冯后来问媒体对基督徒是否不公平. 坎宁安说这取决于视角,但她喜欢看到更多的人说他们是信徒. 她表示:「我觉得有复兴发生, 因为人们在教堂里有过糟糕的经历, 她喜欢看到有大平台的运动员“勇敢而勇敢, 冯说,在过去四年中,他已经认识更多的运动员,似乎有信仰,他有更多的朋友也在努力学习. 他说,“我们想让更多的宗教人物在这里谈论问题。”

title: ‘I Need a Little Gravy on My God’: Kirk Franklin’s New Double Album Is His Answer to 33 Years of Critics
summary: Kirk Franklin’s new album I Am What I Am, his first double album, is out Oct. 30, and he says it is partly an answer to the people who have been questioning his choices for decades. At a listening party in Atlanta, he joked about the whole idea: “I need a little gravy on my…
summary_zh: 柯克·富兰克林（ Kirk Franklin ）的第一张双人专辑《我是我》（ I Am What I Am ）将于10月30日发行，他说，这在一定程度上是对几十年来一直质疑他的选择的人的回答。在亚特兰大的一个倾听派对上，他开玩笑说整个想法： “我需要一点肉汁在我的……
title_zh: “我的上帝需要一点肉汁” ：柯克·富兰克林的新双专辑是他对33年评论家的回答
content: Kirk Franklin’s new album I Am What I Am , his first double album, is out Oct. 30, and he says it is partly an answer to the people who have been questioning his choices for decades. At a listening party in Atlanta , he joked about the whole idea: “I need a little gravy on my God.” The album has 14 songs across two discs, seven studio recordings on the first and seven recorded live on the second. It is Franklin’s 14th studio album, according to the Associated Press, which reports that he is tired of defending his musical decisions. He told the AP he prayed with Chris Brown and Usher before a concert because they asked him to, a moment that drew criticism on social media. “We as believers sometimes become judge and jury,” he said. He also stands by working with GloRilla, whose music is explicit, on the single “This Time.” The song extended his record to 10 No. 1s on Billboard’s Hot Gospel Songs chart, the AP reports. “You start trying to play in other people’s sandboxes, it is going to come with scrutiny,” Franklin said. At the listening party he put it more plainly: “I’ve been trying to explain myself for the last 33 years. This felt like the right opportunity to let people know that I listen and I hear everything that is being said. I am aware. This is my humanity.” Jelly Roll opens the record on “Free Me Tonight,” a spoken-word track the AP says nods to Phil Collins’ “In the Air Tonight.” Franklin reflects on his imperfections and his public criticism on it. Franklin told the AP the song was cathartic and that he once worried it would end his career. “Gospel music is able to handle the raw, unfiltered truth about how ugly and difficult life can be,” he said. On “It Gets Better,” with Tobe Nwigwe, Franklin said at the listening party: “That song was my attempt to find a space to talk about mental health. I’ve had my own journey with anxiety and depression.” He also said, “Living up to the religious standards can create psychological trauma,” and recalled that in his childhood church, young women could be publicly shamed for getting pregnant while the men involved faced no comparable accountability. “Can you imagine the trauma?” he asked. Davido is on “Hope In You,” and Karen Clark Sheard of the Clark Sisters is on the live “Thank You for Everything.” The AP singles out the live “Welcome In,” in which Franklin describes feeling forgotten by God at times while expressing gratitude for God’s steadfast presence. He said the sound of Black church music changed while he was making the album. “The Black church culture changed,” he said. “The church got rid of their choirs and the music was in a space that was not my strength.” Franklin, who is 56 and a 20-time Grammy winner, has no plans to slow down. “The hole that I came from was so deep that whenever I’m around light, I never get tired of feeling the sunlight,” he told the AP.

title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs Says His Touchdown Celebration Is an Ode to the Gospel Song “Break Every Chain,” Not His Recent Arrest
summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says the celebration that set off social media after his latest touchdown was a tribute to a gospel song, not a joke about his recent arrest. In the second quarter of the Packers’ 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers, Jacobs scored on a 1-yard run and briefly put…
summary_zh: 绿湾包装工队跑卫乔什·雅各布斯（ Josh Jacobs ）表示，在他最近一次触地得分后引发社交媒体的庆祝活动是对福音歌曲的致敬，而不是关于他最近被捕的笑话。在包装工队以27-19战胜卡罗莱纳黑豹队的第二节中，雅各布斯在1码的跑步中得分，并简要介绍了......
title_zh: Packers的Josh Jacobs说，他的达阵庆祝活动是对福音歌曲“打破每一条链条”的颂歌，而不是他最近的逮捕
content: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says the celebration that set off social media after his latest touchdown was a tribute to a gospel song, not a joke about his recent arrest. In the second quarter of the Packers’ 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers, Jacobs scored on a 1-yard run and briefly put his hands behind his back while teammates congratulated him. Some viewers watching on television thought he was pretending to be handcuffed. Jacobs said he was modeling the moment after a gospel song called “Break Every Chain.” “The guys did it with me,” he said. “I didn’t think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way. But it’s 2026, and it is what it is.” It was Jacobs’ second game of the season. He had spent time on the NFL’s commissioner’s exempt list after charges were filed against him in August over a May altercation with his then-girlfriend, who said he threw her to the ground. Last month he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He was taken off the list last week and returned to the field, though the league’s investigation is still ongoing. Jacobs said he talked with receiver Savion Williams and other teammates before his season debut, and they planned two celebrations. After his first touchdown of the season, in a 20-17 loss at Detroit, he went to his knees and raised his arms to thank God. The “Break Every Chain” moment was meant for the next one. He also said the broadcast cut away early. “It was more to it than that,” Jacobs said. “They stopped showing the celebration after that.” The NFL’s investigation of Jacobs remains open.
content_zh: Green Bay Packers跑回Josh Jacobs说, 上次触地得分后引发社交媒体的庆典, 在打包员27-19战胜卡罗来纳黑豹队的第二季中,雅各布斯在一码跑道上打入了分数,并短暂地将手放在了背后而队友们向他表示祝贺. 一些在电视上观看的观众认为他假装被铐了. Jacobs说,他正在创作一首名为“打破每一条链子”的福音歌后的瞬间。 他说,“这些家伙是和我一起干的。” “我不认为这会是一种可以被看成是某种方式的东西。 但这是2026年, 这是雅各布斯在该赛季的第二场比赛. 他在8月因5月与当时的女友发生争吵而对他提出指控后,在NFL的免责名单上呆了一段时间,后者说他把她扔倒在地上。 上个月,他没有就殴打和财产损失的轻罪指控提出抗辩。 他上周从名单中除名,回到了球场,尽管联赛的调查仍在进行中. 雅各布斯说他在赛季出道前与接球员萨维翁·威廉斯等队友交谈,两人计划了两次庆祝活动. 在他第一次触地得分后,在底特律的一场20-17失利中,他跪倒并举起手臂感谢上帝. “打破每一条链子”的时刻是下一个时刻。 他还说广播提前中断. Jacobs说,“事情不是那样的。” “此后,他们不再展示庆祝活动。” NFL对Jacobs的调查仍未结束.

title: Pew: Americans Ages 23 to 26 Are Among the Least Religious Adults in the Country, While 18-to-22-Year-Olds Attend Church at Higher Rates Than Anyone
summary: If you’re 25, the Gen Z church revival you keep hearing about may not describe you. Pew Research Center’s newest report on American religion finds that adults ages 23 to 26 are actually the least religious age group in the country on the core measures it tracks, including how often they pray, how much religion…
summary_zh: 如果你25岁，你一直听到的Z世代教会复兴可能无法形容你。皮尤研究中心（ Pew Research Center ）关于美国宗教的最新报告发现， 23至26岁的成年人实际上是该国宗教信仰最少的年龄组，其追踪的核心指标包括他们祈祷的频率、宗教信仰……
title_zh: 皮尤： 23至26岁的美国人是该国宗教信仰最少的成年人，而18至22岁的人参加教会的比率高于任何人
content: If you’re 25, the Gen Z church revival you keep hearing about may not describe you. Pew Research Center’s newest report on American religion finds that adults ages 23 to 26 are actually the least religious age group in the country on the core measures it tracks, including how often they pray, how much religion matters to them and whether they identify with a religion. But the group just below them looks very different. Among adults 18 to 22, 41% say they attend a church, synagogue, mosque or other house of worship at least once or twice a month. That is higher than the 33% for the U.S. public as a whole, and higher than adults born in the 1990s, 1980s, 1970s and 1960s. Among adults 23 to 26, the number is 27%, one of the lowest of any age group. Pew calls the overall picture “complicated,” and the report is careful about what the younger figure can carry. Outside of attendance, the youngest adults are less distinctive. They pray and identify with a religion at lower rates than many older groups. They are no more religious than people that age were in 2014, and by Pew’s measures of prayer, religion’s importance and religious identification, both young groups are significantly less religious than their counterparts in 2007. That said, Pew’s sample is small. The 18-to-22 findings rest on 443 respondents from Pew’s 2025 and 2026 surveys, with a margin of error of plus or minus 5.7 percentage points. Applied to the 41% figure, that is a range of roughly 35% to 47%. Split the group by gender or party and the margins widen further. Pew also notes that this has happened before. In its 2014 Religious Landscape Study, 18-to-22-year-olds attended services at a rate 6 points higher than 23-to-26-year-olds. What is new is that the 2025 and 2026 surveys are the first in which the youngest group is significantly more religious than the next group up on all four of Pew’s core indicators. When the youngest adults have looked more religious in the past, Pew says, the effect has tended to fade with time. It adds that the bump may partly reflect a rebound from the pandemic, and that scholars of religion tend to study change over decades. Some of the details cut against the usual storyline about who is showing up. Young men now attend more often than young women, which Pew says it has not seen before, but 35% of the youngest women attend at least monthly, about the same as women born from the 1950s through the 1980s. Among the youngest Republicans, 55% attend monthly. The youngest Democrats also attend at relatively high rates compared with other Democrats, so Pew says it cannot call this an exclusively Republican phenomenon. Across all ages, Pew finds religion holding steady. The shares who identify with a religion, pray daily, call religion very important and attend monthly have been flat since 2020, and 34% of U.S. adults said in a June survey that they had attended services in person in the previous month, the highest since Pew began asking in 2020. Pew says it has no way of knowing whether the youngest adults will follow the old pattern or break it, and describes the open question as “a turning point or a blip.” If it is a revival, it belongs so far to the very youngest adults in the survey.
content_zh: 若你25岁, 皮尤研究中心关于美国宗教的最新报告发现,23-26岁的成年人实际上是该国在追踪的核心衡量标准上最不信奉宗教的年龄组,包括他们的祈祷次数、宗教对他们的重要性以及他们是否认同某一宗教。 但是他们下面的人群看起来很不一样。 在18至22岁的成年人中,41%的人说,他们每月至少去一次或两次教堂、犹太会堂、清真寺或其他礼拜场所。 这比整个美国公众的33%高,也比1990年代,1980年代,1970年代和1960年代出生的成年人高. 在23至26岁的成年人中,这一数字为27%,是任何年龄组中最低的。 皮尤称总体情况“复杂”,报告对年轻人物能够携带什么十分谨慎。 除了出勤外,最年轻的成年人也不太特别. 他们祈祷和认同宗教的比例低于许多老年群体。 他们的宗教程度不比2014年那个年龄的人多,根据皮尤的祈祷、宗教的重要性和宗教认同措施,2007年,这两个青年群体的宗教程度明显低于同龄人。 皮尤的样本很小。 18至22分的调查结果取自皮尤2025年和2026年调查的443个答卷人,误差幅度为上下5.7个百分点。 适用于41%的数字,约为35%至47%。 按性别或政党划分,差额进一步扩大。 Pew也指出,这以前发生过。 在其2014年的"宗教景观研究"中,18至22岁的青少年参加服务,比23至26岁的青少年高6分. 新情况是,2025年和2026年的调查是第一次最年轻的群体比皮尤所有四个核心指标的下一批群体宗教程度高得多。 当最年轻的成年人在过去看起来更加宗教化时,皮尤说,这种效果往往随着时间逐渐消退. 它还说,这一起伏可能部分反映了该流行病的反弹,宗教学者往往研究几十年来的变化。 一些细节与通常的故事情节相对应, 青年男子现在比青年妇女更经常参加,皮尤说以前从未见过这种活动,但最小的妇女中35%至少每月参加,大约与1950年代至1980年代出生的妇女相同。 在最年轻的共和党人中,有55%每月参加. 与其他民主党人相比,最年轻的民主党人也以相对较高的比率参加,因此皮尤称这不能称之为纯粹的共和党现象. 在所有年龄,皮尤发现宗教是稳定的。 认同某种宗教,每日祷告,呼唤宗教非常重要并每月出席的股份自2020年以来一直是平平的,34%的美国成年人在6月的调查中表示,他们上个月曾亲自参加过各种服务,是皮尤自2020年开始询问以来最高的. Pew说,它无法知道最年轻的成年人是否会遵循旧模式或打破旧模式,并形容这个尚未解决的问题是“一个转折点或一滴一滴地”。 如果是复兴,它迄今为止属于调查中最年轻的成年人。

title_zh: 第一人称：伟大的使命—我们主人的月球射击
content: Portrait of Jeff Ginn, IMB senior ambassador of U.S. and global relations. IMB Photo I was born in 1961. The U.S. president at that time was John F. Kennedy. In that year he issued a challenge to our nation. It was that we build a rocket ship, put men in it, send it to the moon, have them walk on the surface, plant our flag, then return them safely to earth. He called on the nation to accomplish this within a decade. This extraordinary, demanding, costly endeavor is known to history as Kennedy’s “moon shot.” The nation rose to the challenge. I still remember watching in 1969 a grainy, black-and-white broadcast as Neil Armstrong stepped on the surface of the moon and declared, “One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.” We often think of the astronauts with admiration. And rightly so. They were courageous. However, let’s note that the Apollo mission employed some 400,000 additional people to fulfill the mission. Team members included mission controllers, metal fabricators, communication specialists, caterers, engineers, scientists, nurses, doctors, mathematicians and computer programmers. Beyond these, all U.S. taxpayers contributed! It took a nation to get two astronauts to the moon and safely return them! That term, “moon shot,” has made its way into our vocabulary. It can be used for other daring, costly, and valuable undertakings. It is fair, then, to say that the Lord Jesus, our Master, has a moon shot of His own! His mission merits our lives and resources. His mission includes all who name Christ as Lord collaborating to fulfill it. At the International Mission Board, all our plans, strategies and decisions center around this biblical idea that we all must work together to fulfill Christ’s mission. We all must pray. We all must give. We all must go. We all must send. Matthew 28:18-20 is one passage, perhaps the best known, that gives us the details for our mission. The name that evangelicalism has given to this passage is “The Great Commission.” The word “commission” is not one that we use commonly. It simply means a command. How interesting that, with hundreds of commands in Scripture, this is this one that gets the definitive article, “the,” and the adjective, “great.” Does it merit that moniker? I say that it does, and I offer three reasons why. Because it makes a great claim When quoting the Great Commission, it is common for folks to omit verse 18 and simply begin with verse 19. But to do so undercuts the weight that Jesus’ claim in verse 18 adds. There He claims to have all authority in heaven and on earth. That essentially is a claim to divinity — to supremacy. He is saying that He is the King above all kings and the Lord above all lords. When we consider His claim, we all have a choice to make. To borrow from C. S. Lewis, we could decide that He is a liar or a lunatic. Following liberal theologians or Muslim theology, we could decide that much of what is taught about Him in the New Testament is the stuff of legend — that the disciples exaggerated and “created” the Christ of faith. Jeff and Nell Ginn served with the International Mission Board in Colombia. Jeff currently serves churches as IMB senior ambassador. IMB Photo But the decision that I have made (and on which I’ve staked my eternal destiny) is that He is not a liar, nor a lunatic, nor a legend. He is, in fact, Lord! My prayer is that all will decide similarly. As such, He has the authority to issue any commission and our only right response is, “Yes, Lord!” His authority is why, 35 years ago, my wife, Nell, and I said “yes” when He called us to serve with the IMB in Cali, Colombia.  It was under His authority that we planted churches and taught future leaders in the seminary there. Because it gives a great command Not only is it the Great Commission because of the claim that it contains, it is great because of the command it presents.  In verses 19 and 20 there are at least four verbal ideas mentioned: go, make disciples (one word in the origina
content_zh:
美国和全球关系高级大使杰夫·吉恩的肖像. IMB Photo I生于1961年. 当时的美国总统是约翰·肯尼迪. 当年,他向我国提出了挑战。 正是我们造了一艘火箭船,把人装进去,送去月球,让他们行走在地表上,种下我们的旗帜,然后安全地还给地球.

他呼吁全国在十年内完成这项工作. 这一艰巨而昂贵的努力在历史上被称为肯尼迪的"月出"。 国家奋起迎接挑战.

我仍然记得1969年在尼尔·阿姆斯特朗踏上月球时观看了一场黑白交织的广播,并宣布“人类迈出了一小步,人类迈出了一大步”。 我们经常以钦佩的眼光来看待宇航员. 没错 他们是勇敢的。 然而,我们要指出的是,阿波罗飞行任务又雇用了大约40万人来完成这一任务。

小组成员包括特派团控制员、金属制造员、通信专家、宴会人员、工程师、科学家、护士、医生、数学家和计算机程序员。 除此之外,所有美国纳税人都贡献了! 一个民族把两个宇航员送入月球安全送还!. “被射出月球”一词已经进入我们的词汇。

它可用于其他大胆、昂贵和有价值的工作。 那么说上帝耶稣 我们的主人 拥有自己的月球镜头是公平的! 他的使命值得我们给予生命和资源。 他的使命包括所有将基督命名为"主"的人,他们合作完成使命.

在国际传教委员会,我们的所有计划、战略和决定都围绕这个圣经思想,即我们大家必须共同努力来完成基督的使命。 我们都必须祈祷。 我们都必须给予。 我们都得走了。 我们都得送去 Matthew 28: 18 -20是一段,也许最有名的一段,这给我们提供了我们任务的细节.

福音派给这个段落起的名字是“大委员会”。 “委员会”一词不是我们常用的。 这仅仅是命令 如此有趣的是,在《圣经》中有数百个命令, 这篇是获得“the,”和形容词“Great”的决定性文章。 这值得吗? 我说它确实如此,我提出三个原因。

因为它在引用Great Commission(Great Commission)时提出了很大的主张,人们通常省略了第18节,简单地从第19节开始. 但这样做会削弱耶稣在第18节中声称增加的分量。 那边 他声称在天地间拥有一切权威. 这基本上是对神权——至高无上——的宣称。

他说他是国王 高于所有国王 高于所有领主 当我们考虑 他的主张,我们都有一个选择。 从C. S. Lewis那里借钱 我们可以决定他是骗子还是疯子

追随自由主义神学家或穆斯林神学,我们可以决定,"新约"中关于他的大部分教义是传说的东西——门徒夸大并"创造了"信仰的基督. 杰夫和内尔·吉恩在哥伦比亚的国际使团委员会任职。 杰夫目前为教会担任IMB高级大使.

summary: When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. summary_zh: 当大多数"南方浸信会"想到传教士时,他们常常会描绘出教会的植树人和福音派. 但国际使命委员会的领导人说,今天最需要的是那些在幕后工作的专业人员。 咨监委领导人报告说,教师、保健工作者、顾问、会计师、后勤专家和成员护理人员等关键角色正在帮助推进大委员会,许多教会从未看到过。 多琳·贝克,IMB导演
title_zh: IMB寻求教师、医护人员、商业专业人士担任传教士
content: IMB missionary Dr. Heidi Haun, left, checks on patients at Baptist Medical Centre in Nalerigu, Ghana. There are needed roles for IMB missionaries in healthcare, ministering to the needs of local populations and utilizing this time to minister to spiritual needs. IMB Photo When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director of TCK (third culture kid or missionary kid) education, sees a constant need for education professionals. Teachers are needed in international schools, which cover a variety of global educational entities, and in other settings to provide for missionary kids and their educational needs. “Teachers are significant in that not only are they providing instruction for students, but they are an integral part of the core missionary task ,” Baker said. “We also have great needs for consultants to support our families on the field with their children’s education in many ways.” Baker previously served 25 years teaching in Asia and experienced how education creates access to missions where traditional pathways may be limited. IMB missionary Ellie Bohrer teaches a 12th grade World Views class at Black Forest Academy in Germany. The IMB is seeking other educators, like Bohrer, who are willing to use their skills on the mission field. IMB Photo Scott Ray, IMB senior director of global deployment, noted that many missionary positions go unfilled simply because they fall outside traditional perceptions of missionary service. He said professional skills can provide both practical ministry support and access to countries where traditional missionary visas are difficult to obtain. Opportunities exist for finance professionals, veterinarians, medical workers, Send Relief personnel and others. Healthcare remains one of the most strategic areas in demand. Tom Hicks, IMB director of global health strategies, said many medical professionals have the wrong perception about mission work. “We do have an issue where people will select out because they don’t think that what they do is useful on the mission field,” he said. In reality, Hicks said many areas across the globe are increasingly seeking family medicine physicians, internists, pediatricians, pediatric nurse practitioners, OB providers, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech pathologists and lactation consultants. The need is especially significant in sub-Saharan Africa, where young populations create a growing demand for pediatric care. Healthcare professionals also provide a unique advantage in countries that restrict missionary activity. “Missionaries with a vocational value, like healthcare missionaries, have opportunities to go places that others can’t go,” Hicks said. Another often-overlooked ministry is member care, which focuses on the spiritual, emotional, mental and relational health of IMB missionaries. Chris Martin is the IMB director of global member care. “Member care missionaries stand alongside those missionaries that are thought of traditionally as church planters or evangelists and support them,” Martin said. Many who serve in these roles come from counseling backgrounds and help missionaries navigate stress, conflict, grief and other challenges that can affect long-term ministry effectiveness. Martin compares their role to Aaron and Hur in Exodus 19, holding up Moses’ arms during battle, strengthening those serving on the front lines. IMB missionary Glen Garner uses his business skills and experience as the logistics director for missionaries serving globally. He lives in Lima, Peru, with his wife, Shannon

title_zh: IMB传教士通过新信徒和当地教会看到神在工作
content: In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo Twenty minutes had passed already. The sun was going down, and they were looking everywhere, but they only saw men in the park. Sophia, an International Mission Board missionary, joined another IMB missionary and Maryam, a South Asian Christian. They went to the park to share the gospel, but approaching a man in their Muslim-majority city was out of the question. They kept walking and watching. Even if they went home without a single conversation, Sophia knew Maryam would want to try again. This woman who had grown up with a distrust of Muslims, now searched a park for a Muslim woman to tell about Jesus. When Sophia first invited her along, Maryam never imagined a Muslim could come to know Jesus. But the more they went out sharing the gospel together, the more God softened her heart. “One day, I found she was sharing in the park by herself, without me,” Sophia said with a laugh. These days, she shares regularly — with classmates, with rickshaw drivers, with women in the park, when she can find them. God transformed Maryam’s heart. He could transform this walk through the park, too. “So we stopped,” Sophia said, “and prayed, ‘God, give us just one woman to talk to.’” Then they spotted her — a girl sitting alone on a bench. Meeting the girl on the bench She looked like other conservative Muslim women in the area, covered in black except for her face. They approached casually, not wanting to frighten her. It was Eid al-Adha – “one of the biggest Muslim holidays here,” Sophia said. They greeted her and asked about her holiday plans. Her name was Tara, and she wasn’t intimidated at all. “You may think I’m a Muslim from the way I dress,” she said, “but actually in my heart, I have left Islam.” “I was a little shocked,” Sophia said, hearing such a bold statement from a stranger. Tara told them she was a university student at a conservative Islamic school, but she had grown disillusioned and discontent with the religion. “ I don’t believe in Islam anymore,” Tara said. Without knowledge of God, she had no one to pray to, and it left her lonely. She’d been searching — Buddhism and Hinduism from friends, even a meeting with atheists, who struck her as unhappy, following only themselves. “Do you know any Christians?” Sophia asked. “Would you like to hear what we believe?” “Sure, please share.” They read about Jesus’ birth, and Tara was hungry for more. When she asked about church, Sophia described their congregation of about 40 believers, many from a Muslim background. Though she wasn’t ready to visit the church, Tara continued her interest in learning. Sophia and Maryam met with her every week in coffee shops, tea shops, Sophia’s home, wherever they could talkthat wasn’t too loud or have “too many ears and eyes” observing them. Finding her closest friend They read through the Gospel of John. One November day in a coffee shop, they reached the passage on the Samaritan woman at the well, and Sophia noticed Tara was crying. “Tara, I see you have tears,” Sophia said. “Let’s stop. Let’s talk about it .” That day, Tara prayed to receive Christ. Soon after, she wanted to visit the church, though nervous how believers would receive her in a hijab. “They will love you,” Sophia told her. “Don’t worry.” Tara went and was welcomed. That Christmas, 80 people packed Sophia’s apartment, singing and dancing in circles. Across the room, Sophia saw Tara, wearing red Christmas garland like a scarf and a smile stretched across her face. “Tara grew up very conservative – music was not even allowed in her home. But now she’s dancing, worshiping the Lord with us with music and songs.” In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo That spring, Tara was baptized.

title_zh: 神通过IMB在意大利的传教士保持忠诚
content: The eastern face of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City in Rome, Italy, is famous for its central balcony from which popes give their papal addresses. Most people in Rome have at least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” IMB Photo In the city where Jason and Lizzy Davis serve, some steps have a lot of meaning. And the meaning is different for them than it is for the thousands who travel there to visit that site. “If you come to Rome, you can come to a place called the Holy Steps,” Jason said. “People go there, and they’ll crawl up on their knees and pray the rosary all the way up.” From the top of the steps, a mural depicting Jesus on the Cross looks down on those making the pilgrimage. For Jason and Lizzy, it’s a spiritual experience, a picture of a religion that asks people to earn their way to Jesus. “That’s really the opposite of what the gospel is. The gospel is Jesus saying, ‘No, you can’t do it . . . no matter how good you think you are,’” they said. Most people in Rome have at the very least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism, as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” Jason explained, “It’s where the Pope lives in the Vatican. It’s very much part of the religion and culture. It’s all intertwined here.” An ‘unavoidable’ call Jason and Lizzy are investing their lives as International Mission Board missionaries in Rome, Italy, to share the truth of the gospel. The Davises partner with national believers through a new church plant, and they’re seeking to plant more churches within the city. Lizzy said for her, the call to missions was unavoidable. “I grew up as a third culture kid, or a missionary kid. My parents were on the mission field, as were my grandparents, all with the International Mission Board.” Then her family moved to Virginia for her dad to work for IMB’s home office staff. As a middle schooler and high schooler, every time Lizzy heard about the need for the gospel to go forth, she felt a burden, a “burning” in her heart. She didn’t know what God would do with that, but she had a feeling she would see one day. Now, years later, she and Jason spend their time trying to find as many opportunities as they can to invite people into their home so they can share the hope of Jesus with them. That can mean Bible study or simply sharing a meal. ‘Completely lost’ Jason has been surprised by just how often people are willing to talk about faith. “You can get into spiritual conversations very quickly with people, especially if you’re just open and honest with them.” Lizzy shared that one of the easiest ways to do this is to be willing to let your day be interrupted. “That’s something I’ve seen Jason do firsthand in our neighborhood. He walks down the street, and everybody knows him because he stops and takes the time to ask them questions about their families, gets to know people, gets to know the newspaper stand guy and the guy at the fruit stand and the grocery store ladies.” She emphasized that caring about people is “what Christ would do.” The Davises, whose previous mission service prevents their photos from being published, live in a neighborhood of about 130,000 people. Their church of 15 people is the only evangelical congregation there. Lizzy said the area is “truly a lost, completely lost, dark neighborhood” with people who have never heard the gospel. Thousands more come to their area on a religious quest. The Davis family’s neighborhood is home to the Basilica Papale di San Paolo (the Papal Basilica of Saint Paul), one of the city’s four major basilicas. “So we get a lot of people coming on spiritual journeys, visiting our neighborhood, seeking some sort of spiritual experience. And oftentimes it’s just trying to earn their salvation,” she added. Jason described this environment as “a genuine need for people to actually hear the gospel and know that their sins can be forgiven and they can have an assurance of that.” IMB missionaries Jason and Liz

title_zh: 全球传教士合作伙伴通过IMB团队扩展福音工作
content: Rebeca Couto poses with her IMB teammates. Couto is a global missionary partner serving alongside IMB missionaries in Japan. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto poses with her violin. Couto is a professional violinist who is serving as a global missionary partner with the IMB in Japan. Doors have opened for her to use her skills with evangel ical Japanese musicians who perform. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto moved from one volcanic archipelago to another, leaving Portugal’s Azores islands to anchor her life in Japan. The percentage of evangelical Christians in the Azores and Japan is similar, with both populations under 1%. Couto is a fourth-generation Christian, a rarity on the small islands. She is one of few, if any, believers in the Azores with such a long spiritual lineage. This rich legacy shaped her and prepared her for ministry. “I’ve always understood the Great Commission as a call for all believers and all disciples of Christ to be missionaries, wherever they are, whatever they’re doing, and whatever God has equipped them with,” Couto said. Couto’s great-grandfather became a Christian through the witness of missionaries from the United Kingdom. Later, missionaries from the Foreign Mission Board, now the International Mission Board, started the first Baptist work in the Azores by planting an English-speaking church near an American military base. A Baptist Brazilian couple planted a Portuguese-speaking church, which became the congregation where Couto grew up and was commissioned as a missionary. Ministry has been passed down through the generations of her family. Couto’s father has pastored for 20 years, and both of her parents have been involved in ministry for most of their lives. Couto now serves in Japan as a global missionary partner, a missionary who is financially supported by a sending church or organization in their home country and serves with IMB teams. Close to 400 GMPs currently serve on IMB teams around the world. Language learning Couto is immersed in language study in Yokohama, Japan. She had a head start before she even arrived. After graduating from high school, Couto moved from the Azores to Lisbon to pursue a degree in music. She spent hours on public transportation and wanted a challenge to pass the time. She decided to study Japanese because she thought it sounded beautiful. At the time, she had no intention of becoming a missionary in the traditional sense. However, the more she learned about the language and the culture, her burden for the lost grew. She began researching Christianity in Japan. “I understood how bleak the scenario was, and how much the country needed Jesus. I struggled with that calling because the doors were closed, and it didn’t seem possible to come to Japan for a myriad of reasons,” Couto said. After finishing master’s degrees in music and violin performance, along with a seminary degree, Couto was considering pursuing a Ph.D. or returning to seminary when her seminary professors, IMB missionaries Jonathan and Bethany Sharp, contacted her about serving as a missionary in Japan. They introduced her to the GMP program and invited her to attend a missions immersion school they piloted . Rebeca Couto (far right) poses with her IMB teammates. Couto is a global missionary partner serving alongside IMB missionaries in Japan. She continued, “Music is such a universal way to connect with people, and it’s so intuitive to pair that with the gospel and with God’s message to people’s hearts.” While she knew the Lord would somehow open a door for her to use the violin for kingdom work, she was at peace with the possibility that, for a season, she may not be as

title_zh: IMB传教士使用家庭、咖啡馆、应用程序为西班牙的福音对话敞开大门
content: Men and women gather to discuss spiritual topics with Caleb and Carina Beaty, International Mission Board missionaries who serve in Madrid. IMB Photo Across Spain, people looking for connection and meaningful conversation turn to the internet to find groups where they can meet others. At a café by the river, Caleb and Carina Beaty engage in conversations about finding purpose, beauty and “what’s wrong with the world.” A website called Meetup allows people to search for groups to meet in person. The description of the Beatys’ group indicates that it discusses spiritual topics. People come expecting to talk about faith, so it’s not a surprise when they arrive. Caleb said he always has a list of questions that begin broadly and funnel into questions such as, “If there were a God …” or “What do you think Christians believe about that?” or “Why do you think religions have such different perspectives?” The Beatys’ goal in these conversations is to work toward deeper worldview questions within 45 minutes to an hour. Most of the people who attend their Meetup group are from Madrid, but they also have conversations with people from other countries. During one Meetup, Caleb and Carina shared how creation was perfect, but sin led to a world separated from the Father. God offers salvation through the death and resurrection of Jesus, they explained. “There are times we’re able to get to a clear gospel presentation with a group of people, and sometimes we’re doing pre-evangelism.” Caleb said. Some repeat attendees who have been attending for more than a year quickly jump to the heart of the discussion. “All right, Caleb, what’s the Bible say about suffering?” they’ll ask. Caleb and Carina then have the opportunity to share the Christian perspective. IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty and their children pose for a photo in a park in Madrid, Spain.  IMB Photo Spain has secularized rapidly since the 1990s, Caleb said. While many may think of it as a Catholic nation, many people do not know the basic tenets of Christianity. “We’ve got all the churches, we’ve got the cathedrals, and they do processions, but the average person on the street does not know anything about the gospel and does not know anything about Jesus,” Caleb said. Younger Spaniards are drawn to their group and are receptive to the gospel because they don’t have a spiritual foundation or know anyone who does. “There’s just this curiosity because, for a lot of them, they’ve never met someone who actually believes that God exists, and that changes your life,” Carina said. “I’ve had people completely shocked that we believe in God. ‘You really believe that God exists?’ They can’t wrap their mind around that.” During one Meetup, a man contrasted Protestant and Catholic beliefs by saying Protestants focus on Jesus’ suffering and Catholics on Mary’s grief. Caleb responded that evangelicals focus on the resurrection. When Caleb said Jesus rose from the dead, the man replied that he needed to look into that. Caleb said encounters like that reveal how little many Spaniards know about the gospel. Caleb noted the irony of the man’s sharing the Catholic perspective without truly understanding it. He is not the only person the Beatys have met who has missed the heart of the gospel. A friend of the Beatys told them she’d heard Jesus died, but she hadn’t heard he rose from the dead. A man reads a passage of Scripture during a Bible study hosted by IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty at their family’s apartment in Madrid, Spain. Five atheists began attending their Bible study after attending the couple’s Meetup group. IMB Photo The Beatys also host seasonal outreach events through the Meetup. Members from their church in Madrid have started attending the Meetup to learn how the Beatys lead discussions. Their group has become so popular, a waitlist has formed. Caleb and Carina host a small-group Bible study in their home. Five atheists who joined their Meetup now attend the Bible study.

IMB President Paul Chitwood said he celebrates what God did in the 2025-26 season and what He is doing now to lead Southern Baptists toward historic generosity. “I thank God for Southern Baptists! Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. Totals in each of the last four years have surpassed $70 million. “I am so grateful to the pastors and churches for the faithfulness and generosity they have demonstrated through this offering,” said NAMB president Kevin Ezell. “As I travel and speak in churches of all sizes, I love seeing the posters in the hallways showing their offering goals. title_zh: 俄克拉荷马州浸信会加入派遣教会实验室，以加强传教士支持
content: Staff members at First Baptist Church in Wagoner, Oklahoma, evaluate their church’s involvement with missions and missionary support. IMB Photo The chapel at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City turned into a science lab on Oct. 5-6. Microscopes, beakers and test tubes weren’t in the room, but this Sending Church Lab drew nearly 40 people representing 12 Oklahoma Baptist churches committed to send and care for international missionaries well. The Sending Church Lab, facilitated by the International Mission Board, brought pastors, church leaders and missionaries together for two days of discussion, self-assessment and planning centered on one question: What does it mean for a church to truly be a sending church? For Mike Wall, a global missions ministry partner of Oklahoma Baptists, the answer begins with churches reclaiming responsibility for the Great Commission. Wall first attended a Sending Church Lab last year in Tulsa with few expectations. He left convinced more churches needed the training. “When I went there, I thought, ‘You’ve got to do this in Oklahoma City,’” Wall said, “because of the content and how much our churches need something just like this.” After observing churches work through the exercises in the lab, Wall said he was encouraged by an emphasis on local church ownership in missions. “We can’t just send our people and say, ‘OK, now this is your job, IMB,’” he said. “We have to do our job in sending, preparing and training the best ‘sent ones’ so that when they get to the field, they can already hit the ground running.” Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement specialist, leads a Sending Church Lab at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City. He is emphasizing the importance of sending churches assessing and equipping future IMB missionaries. IMB Photo Leading the lab was Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement strategist, who developed the concept after seeing the need for stronger relationships between missionaries and local churches. “A Sending Church Lab is our attempt to raise up a host of IMB sending churches,” Wooten said, crediting the North American Mission Board for doing similar events and having successful results. The lab helps churches understand what Wooten calls the church engagement pathway: praying, cooperating, partnering and sending. While many churches faithfully pray, give and go, he said sending requires something more intentional. “Sending includes taking responsibility for an IMB missionary by providing ongoing encouragement, accountability and soul care throughout their term of service,” he explained. During the two-day event, participants gathered around whiteboards to evaluate their church’s missions practices, identify strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement. “We don’t just need to deliver content,” Wooten said. “We need to invite churches to do some work on their own.” Rather than simply listening to presentations, attendees worked through practical questions about prayer, giving, short-term missions, missionary assessment and long-term care. Wooten said churches consistently tell him the greatest benefit is clarity. “They are thankful for clarity on what an IMB sending church is and what our roles and responsibilities are,” he said. For IMB missionaries Peter and Katie Weeks, that clarity is especially valuable. They participated in the lab alongside church leaders. Their real names have been changed to protect their work in Southeast Asia. “There’s no other place I’d rather be during these few days than here,” Peter said. Katie appreciated the interactive nature of the training. “I really appreciate the way they’re actually requiring information from the different churches and encouraging dialogue about how they can go through the steps,” she said. content_zh: 俄克拉何马州瓦戈纳第一浸信会的工作人员评价了教会参与传教和传教活动的情况。 IMB 相片 俄克拉荷马城Constitute Road Baptist Church的小教堂于10月5-6日变成科学实验室. 但这个送信教会实验室吸引了近40人, 代表12个俄克拉何马浸会教会, 传教士实验室在国际传教委员会的协助下,召集牧师、教会领袖和传教士进行两天的讨论、自我评估和规划,其中心是一个问题: 教会真正成为送教之所意味着什么? 对于俄克拉何马浸信会的全球使命部合作伙伴迈克·沃尔来说,答案始于教会重新为大委员会负责。 去年沃尔在图尔萨参加了一个送教实验室, 他离开后确信更多的教会需要训练. “当我去那里时,我想,`你必须在俄克拉荷马城做这件事,'墙说,`因为内容和我们的教会需要这样的东西。 在观察了教堂通过实验室的演练工作后,沃尔说,他在任务中强调当地教会的所有权使他受到鼓舞. “我们不能只是派我们的人来说,“好吧,这是你的工作,IMB。” “我们必须在派遣、准备和训练最优秀的`派遣 ' 人员方面完成我们的工作,这样,当他们到达实地时,他们就已经可以奔跑地了。” Bryan Wooten,IMB高级教会订婚专家,在俄克拉荷马城的Constitution Road Baptist教堂领导一个送教实验室. 他强调派遣教会评估和装备未来的IMB传教士的重要性. IMB Photo Leading the lab是IMB高级教会接触策略师布莱恩·伍滕(Bryan Wooten),他在看到传教士与本地教会之间需要更牢固的关系后发展出这个概念. 伍腾说,“一个派遣教会实验室是我们努力培养许多派遣教会的IMB。 ”他赞扬北美传教委员会开展了类似的活动并取得了成功。 实验室帮助教会理解伍腾所谓的教会参与途径:祈祷,合作,合作和发送. 虽然许多教堂忠实地祈祷,奉献和去,但他说送去需要更有意图的东西. 他解释说,“最后包括负责一个IMB传教士,在整个任职期间提供持续的鼓励、问责和精神关怀。” 在为期两天的活动期间,与会者聚集在白板周围,评价其教会的任务做法,查明优缺点并制订改进计划。 」伍腾说: “我们需要邀请教会自己做一些工作。” 与会者不是简单地听取演讲,而是通过祷告、赠送、短期访问、传教士评估和长期照料等实际问题开展工作。 Wooten说,教会总是告诉他最大的好处是清晰. 他说,“他们感谢对派遣教会的咨监委的澄清,以及我们的作用和责任。” 对于IMB的传教士彼得和凯蒂·威克斯来说,这种清晰度特别有价值. 他们与教会领袖一起参加了实验室. 他们的真名被更改以保护自己在东南亚的工作. 彼得说,“在这几天里,我宁愿呆在这里。” 凯蒂对培训的互动性表示赞赏. 我非常欣赏他们要求不同教会提供信息的方式, 从传教士的角度来看,她认为实验室解决了共同的挑战. title_zh: 数字化之门为东南亚岛民打开福音之门
content: Just as young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than in person, the same is true for people in Southeast Asia. IMB missionaries are creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content to connect with the lost through the internet. IMB Photo Recently, an International Mission Board team in Southeast Asia asked a young woman if she had heard the story of Jesus. She replied that, yes, she had heard about Him through a video online! “Back in the day,” shared Amanda Clarkston, an IMB missionary who has served in Southeast Asia for 33 years, “when I first came on the field, you’d go somewhere and gather all the people together in the village to watch the JESUS film.” Now, face-to-face conversations about Christ on the Southeast Asian islands are harder to accomplish. While teams travel to these remote islands often, living in a sparsely populated, animistic background culture as a foreigner creates suspicion and make long-term ministry difficult. Furthermore, young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than they are in person, Clarkston said, which is true of the islanders as well. Attempting to have a spiritual conversation face-to-face has become “too much” for locals, Clarkston shared. So, how do you share the gospel with multiple people groups who are constantly online and less comfortable with in-person interactions? For these Southeast Asia teams, digital engagement — the use of social media platforms to share a message — has become a plausible and effective entry point. The social media agency We Are Social confirmed this, revealing that 82.4% of Southeast Asia’s population uses the internet. “No matter where they go, how far they go, how remote it is, people have phones,” Clarkston and her team realized, “And though sometimes they do have to climb up the highest peak to get reception, people do it.” Clarkston’s team has begun creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content in hopes of building bridges to the islanders through the internet. Viewers can click on the ad to message back and forth with a responder, a local believer or missionary who is available to pray, build relationships and answer spiritual questions. “It seems like locals are more open to watching those things in the privacy of their own cell phones,” Clarkston said. Clarkston intends to use digital engagement as a means for initial contact with people with animistic backgrounds, evangelism and, eventually, discipleship. She said that this new ministry has the potential to open doors with individuals across these islands who would normally never reach out on their own or respond to the gospel in person. “Maybe they’ll respond this way,” Clarkston said, “I know without a shadow of a doubt that God is calling people to Himself.” Now, more than ever, technology has a grip on society. Many spend hours each day mindlessly scrolling, searching for meaning, for happiness. And now, more than ever, there is an incredible opportunity to plant seeds across Southeast Asian islands through digital engagement. The IMB Southeast Asia team gives praise to the Lord that He has provided a creative way to reach the lost and plant seeds. Pray the people among the Southeast Asian islands would see these ads and engage with responders boldly, even though they may face persecution or harm because of it. Names were changed for security. Mikah Young is serving overseas with the IMB. The work of the IMB is sustained through faithful giving to the Cooperative Program and the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering ® . Clarkston说, “当地人似乎更愿意在手机的隐私中观看这些东西。 克拉克斯顿打算用数字化的接战作为与有动画背景,福音派,并最终有门徒身份的人进行初步接触的手段. 她说,这个新的部有可能对这些岛屿上的个人敞开大门,他们通常不会独自伸出援手或亲自回应福音。 “也许他们会以这种方式回应,”克拉克斯顿说,“我毫不怀疑地知道,上帝正在号召人们投靠自己。 ” 现在,技术比以往更加控制社会。 许多人每天花上数小时无所顾忌地滚动,寻找意义,追求幸福. 现在,比以往任何时候,通过数字化参与,在东南亚各岛屿播种种子的机会比以往任何时候都多。 IMB东南亚队称赞了"主",他为到达失落地并播下种子提供了创造性的方法. 请东南亚各岛屿人民看到这些广告,并大胆地与回应者接触,尽管他们可能因此而面临迫害或伤害。 更改了安全名称。 米卡·杨在IMB海外服役. title_zh: IMB传教士在服务之旅中分享首尔的愿景
content: Ask most people what comes to mind when they think of South Korea, and they’ll likely mention K-pop, skincare, cutting-edge technology, or bustling city streets filled with young professionals. Hun and Eunjoo Sol see those things too. But after more than a decade serving as International Mission Board missionaries in Seoul, they also see something many visitors never notice. “Many people think that Korea is exciting and successful,” Hun said. “They think about the K-pop, the K-culture, K-technology, K-cosmetics. Yes, good things… But many Korean people are struggling right now.” The Sols, who were featured in the 2025 Week of Prayer for International Missions , continue to rely on the prayers of faithful Southern Baptists. Prayers sustain them and help to push back the darkness they confront in their home culture. Hun often describes that hidden struggle with a Korean word: han. There is no simple English translation. It speaks to a deep sorrow shaped by generations of war, division, loss, and the quiet resolve to endure. Hun sees it in the young adults he meets every week—people navigating loneliness and relentless expectations, quietly asking what their lives are for beneath a veneer of success. Han is heavy. For many young adults, that weight can feel unbearable. Suicide is one of the leading causes of death among teenagers and young adults in South Korean. Hun and Eunjoo see the effects of that reality every day, and it’s one reason they believe they have no time to waste. That understanding shaped the week of Serve Tour Seoul this summer. There were no construction sites, no paintbrushes, no tools or work gloves. Instead, the team stepped into ministries local churches had been faithfully building long before the volunteers arrived. In May, 27 volunteers from seven churches across the United States came alongside local churches already serving their communities in Seoul, Paju, and Gwangju. They taught English classes, ran children’s camps, walked neighborhoods in prayer, distributed food, and sat down with college students, one conversation at a time. For Nick Holst of Sandals Church in Riverside, California, the goal was simple enough to say in a sentence: “We came to meet people,” Holst said. “We want to hear their stories, and that leads to some very meaningful connections as you get past the surface into something deeper.” That’s where the week actually lived: past the surface and past the small talk, where the quiet weight of han is often carried without words. On college campuses, volunteers played games, asked questions and mostly just listened. Some conversations lasted a few minutes and ended there. Others kept going long past the point where either person expected them to. One morning, after asking his church back home to pray, Holst sat down with a university student named Intec. They talked about culture first, the way strangers do, and then the conversation turned somewhere neither of them planned. “I got to ask him, ‘What do Koreans believe?’” Holst recalled. Intec said he didn’t believe in God. Then he recited John 3:16 from memory, word for word, a verse he’d heard somewhere along the way and never forgotten. Before they parted, Holst asked if he could pray that God would keep drawing Intec toward Himself. “He said yes.” In a city where many conversations never move beyond the surface, the exchange was a reminder of why the team had come. Not to win an argument, but to listen, to ask questions, and to trust God with what happens next. The same pattern unfolded elsewhere, beginning in classrooms and ending on city streets. Jeremy Doyle, missions pastor at Valley Baptist Church in Bakersfield, California, watched an English conversation club grow from two students on its first night to eight by the second. Nobody advertised it as anything more than a place to practice English, but the room kept filling, and so did the conversations. The team’s work with students didn’t stop there. title: 从敬拜领袖到杀妻凶手
summary: 贪婪不只是贪钱，也可能是贪恋地位、名声，以及掌控一切的感觉。一桩令人震惊的杀妻案提醒我们：当人既想满足私欲，又不肯承担后果，就可能亲手毁掉自己原本拥有的幸福。
content: 他看上去是个好基督徒。事实上，他还是一位带领敬拜的平信徒长老。俄亥俄州二月的夜晚寒气逼人，他那不起眼的家却温暖而寻常，两个年幼的女儿还在屋里熟睡。然而，警方执法记录仪拍下的画面，与这一切形成了强烈反差。他惊慌失措，泣不成声，身穿印有“与神的大能相称的异象”（God-Sized Vision）字样的卫衣，告诉警察：窃贼闯进家里，开枪打死了躺在床上的妻子，然后逃走了。 但这套说辞经不起查证。曾参加《美国偶像》（American Idol）的凯勒布·弗林（Caleb Flynn），于 9 月 29 日被判谋杀妻子罪成立。大量证据表明，他一心想除掉妻子，好与婚外情对象在一起；对方也是他所在教会的一名领唱歌手。 庭审视频显示，律师宣读了弗林与情人之间的短信，其中流露出盼着他妻子死去的念头。弗林坐在那里，始终面无表情。在他被判终身监禁、不得假释前几分钟，妻子的家人 向他宣读了女儿们写来的信 。 那一刻，弗林仿佛尝到了一点真实的地狱滋味：那些曾经爱他的人，用自己的话提醒他，他永远失去了什么。这些话，也成了对他所作所为的公正审判。 一个带领敬拜的人，怎么会走到这一步？ 从贪婪走向谋杀 有人会说，是情欲。他们没说错。任何基督徒都不该低估不正当幻想的力量。我们任由想象沉溺其中，迟早就会想要付诸行动。奸淫会带来毁灭性的后果。难怪所罗门要儿子想一想：“人若怀里搋火，衣服岂能不烧呢？”（ 箴 6:27 ） 但如果只看见情欲，就漏掉了其他问题。情欲可以解释他为什么背弃婚约，却未必能解释他为什么扣下扳机。这个身穿“与神的大能相称的异象”卫衣的男人，将在监狱里度过余生，不只是因为情欲，也是因为贪婪。 在美国，对婚姻不满的人几乎可以出于任何理由提出离婚。无论从法律、政治还是现实条件来看，都没有什么使弗林不能与情人在一起，而必须留在妻子身边。即使离婚，他也极有可能仍能与妻子共同享有女儿的监护权。 那么，为什么阿什莉·弗林（Ashley Flynn）“非死不可”？因为发起离婚意味着他必须承认自己的奸淫，不仅向妻子承认，也要向周围所有人承认。他必须离开主日敬拜的聚光灯，也会失去在岳父手下那份收入丰厚的工作。 我们无法看透弗林的内心，也无法完全了解他复杂的动机。但我怀疑，他想要的是婚外情，却不愿付出婚外情的代价。 贪婪不易察觉 许多人都知道，情欲多么善于欺骗人。但对不少福音派信徒来说，贪婪却是一条更难揪出来的蛇。一个原因是，贪婪不像情欲，贪婪可以披上美德的外衣。一个基督徒若被教会里的弟兄姊妹看见自己的色情浏览记录，会感到羞耻；但如果他为了事业野心不顾一切，却很可能期待大家支持、肯定他。 贪婪有时藏得很深。一听到这个词，我们很容易只想到守财奴埃比尼泽·斯克鲁奇（Ebenezer Scrooge，《圣诞颂歌》主角）：办公室冷得像冰窖，他却不许鲍勃·克拉奇特（Bob Cratchit）添火取暖。但贪婪不只是贪钱，也包括紧抓着自己的身份和成就不放。 一位知名牧师犯下足以使他失去牧职资格的罪，起初也表达了懊悔，为什么却不能在余生中安静、谦卑地悔改，不再追求出头露面？很多时候，是因为他贪恋领袖和讲道人受人敬重的身份。他无法想象，失去牧职带来的地位与待遇，自己还能怎样生活；就像斯克鲁奇无法想象，自己怎么能多拿出一点钱帮助穷人。 也有另一种可能：至今仍未认罪的弗林以为，只要控制住后果，就能让罪显得没那么严重。我不知道，他是否曾这样说服自己：杀死妻子，就能让她免受背叛与离婚之苦。也许，他甚至荒谬地把自己看成了英雄，宁可让自己的良心背上污点，也不让妻子承受被抛弃的痛苦。 如果真是这样，那也是贪婪：他贪求掌控一切，不愿承受自己的选择所带来的后果。如果弗林任由奸淫带来的后果显露，哪怕最终婚姻破裂，他也可能在其中遇见恩典，回转悔改。浪子本不该离家，但落到与猪争食的境地，却使他回了头。相比之下，犹大没有给自己机会，去知道彼得也曾背叛主。如果他愿意承受羞耻和耻辱，而不是以自杀逃避，也许他也会听见主问：“你爱我吗？” 掌控和金钱一样，都是我们急于得到的东西；一旦觉得自己有了一点，就又想得到更多。德国哲学家哈特穆特·罗萨（Hartmut Rosa）认为，现代社会追逐金钱与追求掌控的方式十分相似。但当我们接受 世界并不尽在掌握之中 ，就会发现，那些让生活充满不安的事，也恰恰使生活有了意义。无法掌控一切固然令人害怕，却也让我们有机会被触动、被改变，并从中蒙福。 贪婪最大的谎言 贪婪最大的谎言就是让人相信，唯有牢牢抓住，才能真正拥有。因此，我们需要不断提醒自己两件事：我们无法掌控一切；而那位掌管一切的主，虽然悉心照料祂所造的世界，却更加顾念我们。 贪婪的谎言终究会被揭穿。对弗林而言，揭穿谎言的是 女儿们的话 。其中一个女儿在信中写道： 妈妈是个完美的人，真的完美极了。她究竟做错了什么，让你那么恨她？ 她爱你，关心你，照顾你。她全心全意地爱着你。 她是我最好的朋友。可你却选择杀死我唯一的妈妈。我真的好想她，好想、好想、好想她。你根本不知道我有多想她。 女儿看得明白：父亲不是太渴望幸福，而是他所追求的幸福太狭小了。贪婪不只扭曲了他的心，毒害了他的行为，也蒙蔽了他的眼睛。 但女儿仍不肯放弃他。她在信的结尾写道：“记住，你还有机会。你总还有选择。我希望你能重新让耶稣住进你的心里。” 如今，凯勒布·弗林已失去一切掌控，余生都将在监狱中度过。然而，只要他还不肯悔改、认罪、领受神的恩典，就仍是贪婪的囚徒。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Caleb Flynn and the Deadly Sin of Greed .
author: Samuel James

title: Alliance seeks next Executive Director
summary: In a time of global challenge and opportunity, the Wycliffe Global Alliance is searching for its next Executive Director.
summary_zh: 在这个充满全球挑战和机遇的时代，威克理夫全球联盟正在寻找下一任执行董事。
title_zh: Alliance寻求下一任执行董事
content: God’s Word transforms lives, strengthens churches and brings hope across generations. Bible translation is part of that story, as communities around the world encounter God’s Word in their own languages. Its future calls for leaders who listen deeply, build trust across cultures and empower others. Within this context, the Wycliffe Global Alliance is searching for its next Executive Director. Could this be your next calling? The Wycliffe Global Alliance is seeking its next Executive Director to serve a worldwide community of more than 100 organisations united in God’s mission through Bible translation. Th e opportunity : Bring our global community together around a shared vision, strengthen local leadership and help a diverse global movement respond to new opportunities with faith and wisdom. The challenge : Lead through change. Articulate a compelling shared vision, strengthen the support the Alliance offers its organisations, and engage support organisations and financial partners in advancing the work. This calls for leadership that honours local autonomy while strengthening global unity, trust, mutual accountability and financial sustainability. We are looking for a leader who brings: A deep commitment to Jesus Christ and a humble, prayerful approach to leadership. At least five years of senior leadership experience and a relevant master’s degree. Proven ability to lead across cultures, develop leaders and empower local churches. Strategic vision, significant fundraising experience and the ability to turn plans into meaningful outcomes. Emotional maturity, integrity and resilience through change. Feel called—or know someone who might be? Expressions of interest, or candidate recommendations, are welcomed confidentially by 30 November 2026 . More info: full profile and how to respond
content_zh: 神之道会改变生活,加强教堂,并带来世代相传的希望. 圣经翻译是这个故事的一部分,因为世界各地的社区都用自己的语言遇到上帝的话语。 它的未来要求领导人深刻倾听,在不同文化之间建立信任并赋予他人权力。 在这方面,威克里夫全球联盟正在寻找其下任执行主任。 这会不会是你的下一个电话? Wycliffe全球联盟正在寻求下一任执行主任,通过圣经翻译服务于100多个组织联合起来执行上帝的使命。 机会:把我们的全球社会团结在一个共同的愿景周围,加强地方领导,帮助一个多样化的全球运动以信念和智慧应对新的机遇。 挑战:领导变革。 阐述令人信服的共同愿景,加强联盟为各组织提供的支持,并让支助组织和金融伙伴参与推进这项工作。 这要求发挥领导作用,尊重地方自治,同时加强全球团结、信任、相互问责和财政可持续性。 我们要找一位领导,他带来: 对耶稣基督的深刻承诺和谦卑而虔诚的领导方式. 具有至少五年的高级领导经验和相关的硕士学位. 证明有能力领导不同文化,培养领导人并增强地方教会的能力。 战略愿景、大量筹资经验和将计划转化为有意义的成果的能力。 情感成熟,完整性和通过变化的韧性. 感觉被叫了... 还是认识一个人? 在2026年11月30日之前,以保密方式欢迎表示兴趣或候选人建议。 更多信息:完整简介和如何应对

title: Wycliffe Global Alliance Communications Workshop – Africa Area
summary: This project seeks to equip trainers who can contextualise and deliver OBT training within Latin America
summary_zh: 该项目旨在为培训师提供能够在拉丁美洲范围内提供OBT培训的背景知识
title_zh: 威克里夫全球联盟传播研讨会–非洲地区
content: Communication staff at 18 Bible translation organizations across Africa need professional training to tell God’s stories well. In November 2026, a one-week workshop in Ruiru, Kenya will teach practical skills like writing, photography, design and video. Then, six months of follow-up support will continue to strengthen networks and create a collaborative culture of sharing God’s stories widely and effectively. Project Name: Africa Area Communication Capacity Building Workshop Implementing Organization: Wycliffe Global Alliance – Africa Area Contact: Phil Prior Director for Communication Wycliffe Global Alliance phil_prior@wycliffe.net Matthew Bore Project Funding Manager Wycliffe Global Alliance matthew_bore@wycliffe.net Start date: September 2026 End date: March 2027 Summary Across Africa, God is moving. Communities are receiving the Bible in their own language for the first time. Lives are being transformed. But too often, these stories never become known beyond the place where they happen. Why? Because not enough people are trained to recognise and report these stories to a wider audience. Among 18 Bible translation organisations across Africa, communication staff are doing their best—but without formal training in news writing, interviewing, photography, video and social media. Many also work in relative isolation without the chance to exchange ideas and collaborate on stories. The result: Amazing stories remain untold, and the people who could be praying, giving or getting involved never learn about the opportunities. This project changes that. For one week (2-6 November 2026) in Ruiru, Kenya, communication staff from those 18 Wycliffe Global Alliance organisations will come together — not just to sit in a classroom, but to actually create. Using smartphones and free tools, they will learn to capture the moments that matter: local communities and churches collaborating; a translation team’s challenges and creative solutions, groups engaging with Scripture, lives being transformed. Attendees also will build plans for how their organisations will keep telling these types of stories long after the workshop ends. Then, over the ensuing six months, this same group will keep coaching, encouraging, and learning from each other — turning 18 separate voices into one strong, unified story of what God is doing across Africa. title: Training Oral Translators Across Southeast Asia
summary: This project seeks to equip trainers who can contextualise and deliver OBT training within Latin America
summary_zh: 该项目旨在为培训师提供能够在拉丁美洲范围内提供OBT培训的背景知识
title_zh: 在东南亚培训口译员
content: A three-year training program will prepare local translators across Southeast Asia to put the Bible into spoken forms—like storytelling and song—for communities that share knowledge by voice, not writing. Three workshops will build translators’ skills from basic to advanced to mentoring, so at least 20 participants gain local expertise. Project Name: Training Oral Translators Across Southeast Asia Implementing Organization: Wycliffe Global Alliance Contact: Evelyn Gan Consultant for Oral Translation Programmes Wycliffe Global Alliance evelyn_gan@wycliffe.net Start date: FY 2026 End date: FY 2028 Summary Across Southeast Asia, many communities pass along their culture through spoken word—storytelling, song, and drama—rather than through reading and writing. For them, hearing the Bible in these natural forms often connects more deeply than a printed text. Oral Bible Translation is expanding rapidly in Southeast Asia, but the region lacks enough trained people to sustain it. Seminary graduates know the Bible but not oral translation. Practitioners already working need a path to advance their skills. And almost no one is ready to step into consultant roles. Without urgent, structured training, this shortage could stall Oral Bible Translation projects across the region. This three-year project will trains local translators and seminary students in oral Bible translation. Participants move through three stages: a foundation workshop, an advanced workshop and consultant-level training, with only those who show strong skills advancing to the next stage. Our goal is for at least 20 participants, with a smaller group becoming fully qualified to guide future translation projects. Half of the trainers will themselves be new, gaining experience so the program can continue and grow after this project ends. By working in collaboration with Wycliffe Thai Foundation, Wycliffe Malaysia, YWAM Chiang Mai, FCBH, Spoken Worldwide and CRU, the project is rooted in strong partnerships that will ensure sustainability and local ownership. title: Training Oral Translators in Indonesia

content: Indonesia has hundreds of languages still without Scripture in natural, spoken forms. This three-year program will train 20 local translators and seminary students to fill that gap, building skills from basic to advanced to mentoring. Working with local partners, it aims to grow into a lasting, homegrown training network. Project Name: Training Oral Translators in Indonesia Implementing Organization: Wycliffe Global Alliance Evelyn Gan Consultant for Oral Translation Programmes Wycliffe Global Alliance evelyn_gan@wycliffe.net Start date: FY 2026 End date: FY 2028 Summary Indonesia is home to hundreds of languages whose speakers pass on knowledge through spoken word rather than writing. Most still lack the Bible in a form that feels natural to hear. Oral Bible Translation is expanding quickly in Indonesia, but training hasn’t kept up—seminary graduates lack oral translation skills, and working practitioners have no path to grow or reach consultant-level readiness. Without urgent, structured training, projects across the country risk stalling. This three-year project trains local translators and seminary students to close that gap. Participants move through three stages—foundational, advanced and consultant-level training—with those who show strong skills advancing to the next stage. Our goal is for at least 20 participants, with a smaller group becoming fully qualified to guide future translation projects on their own. The project partners with several Indonesian organizations, including seminaries, so that this training becomes part of local theological education rather than a one-time effort. That partnership is central to the goal: building lasting, Indonesian-led capacity so that projects no longer depend on outside experts.
