title: Bible translation’s future is diverse … and local
summary: The ultimate metric of success is no longer just the distribution of physical books, but measurable transformation of lives through deep, culturally authentic understanding.
summary_zh: 衡量成功的最终标准不再仅仅是实体书籍的分发，而是通过深刻的文化真实理解对生活进行可衡量的转变。
title_zh: 圣经翻译的未来是多元化的……和本地
content: Yaoundé, Cameroon — The landscape of global Bible translation is undergoing a paradigm shift, moving away from traditional, agency-led book printing and toward multimodal translations driven by local communities. At a June 2026 gathering in Yaoundé, translation partners and members of Wycliffe Global Alliance organisations spanning Africa, Europe and Latin America reflected on how Scripture is delivered in the 21st century. Their consensus: The ultimate metric of success is no longer just the distribution of physical books, but measurable transformation of lives through deep, culturally authentic understanding. Community-led translation Dr. Paul Kimbi, the Alliance’s Consultant for Bible Translation Programmes, said Bible translation’s future belongs to community dialogue rather than isolated translation agencies. This emerging approach, known as conversational translation, prioritises localised, grassroots work: listening intimately to communities, engaging them in active storytelling and using locally adapted communication channels. As multiple translation agencies increasingly operate within the same borders, global leaders are urging a shift toward radical collaboration. ‘The multiplicity of agencies is not a hindrance; however, harmony and unity are essential,’ Kimbi said. ‘Unity does not mean uniformity. Each agency, according to its unique strengths, approaches Bible translation as a collaborative piece of God’s global mission.’ Multimodal translations will better serve people from different contexts . Beyond the Book: Multimodal and AI Integration Because cultural contexts vary wildly across the globe, the Alliance’s Africa Area gathering highlighted the urgent need for ‘embodied and multimodal’ translations. This means managing multiple streams of communication simultaneously—integrating oral storytelling, vibrant illustrations, written text and digital media. ‘We do not communicate only with words; we communicate with colours, images, and multimedia,’ Kimbi said. ‘We can no longer consider translation strictly as a written book, but rather as a dynamic multimodal experience.’ This digital evolution naturally intersects with the rise of artificial intelligence. While delegates recognised AI’s immense potential to increase translation speed, optimise efficiency and lower operational costs for minority languages, attendees maintained a stance of strategic caution. ‘Technology accelerates the advancement of Bible translation and language development, but it also creates new strategic responsibilities for leaders and organisations,’ said Etienne Ondoa, a language technology consultant. Staff capacity building, therefore, remains the greatest investment, he said. As technology evolves, the skills required to support it in ministry also evolve. ‘Technological leadership should have a voice in strategic decision-making processes, Ondoa said. ‘Technological decisions increasingly influence ministry outcomes, sound financial resource management, cybersecurity, AI adoption and organisational resilience.’ Etienne Ondoa A Symphony for the Global Church Ultimately, leaders at the event reaffirmed that translation organisations do not operate in a vacuum. They exist to serve the church, which remains God’s primary vehicle for global mission. Kimbi likened the future of the movement to a grand, global arrangement. ‘The particularity of modern Bible translation is that it is a diverse ensemble—an orchestra of varied influences interpreting a magnificent symphony titled ‘Scriptures’ for every language community,’ he said. ‘And in this orchestra, we need everyone: local churches, oral communicators, media creators, literacy specialists and technology partners.’ Story: Lune Prudence Mvondo and Isaac Forchie Photos: Isaac Forchie
content_zh: 喀麦隆雅温得 全球圣经翻译的地貌正在发生范式转变,从传统的、机构主导的书籍印刷转向由当地社区驱动的多模式翻译。 在2026年6月的雅温得集会上,翻译伙伴和遍布非洲、欧洲和拉丁美洲的维克利夫全球联盟组织的成员反思了21世纪如何交付《圣经》。 他们的共识: 衡量成功与否的终极尺度不再仅仅是物理图书的发行,而是通过深刻,文化上真实的理解,对生活进行可测量的转变. 联盟的圣经翻译方案顾问Paul Kimbi博士说,圣经翻译的未来属于社区对话而不是孤立的翻译机构。 这种新兴方法被称为对话翻译、地方化优先化、基层工作:密切听取社区的意见,让他们参与积极讲故事,并使用适合当地情况的交流渠道。 随着多个翻译机构越来越多地在同一边界内运作,全球领导人正在敦促向根本合作转变。 Kimbi说 : “ 机构繁多并非障碍, `团结并不意味着统一。 每个机构都根据其独特的长处,将圣经翻译视为上帝全球使命的合作作品。 多式联运将更好地为来自不同背景的人服务。 除了《书:多式联运和人工智能一体化》之外,由于世界各地的文化背景大相径庭,联盟的非洲地区会议强调迫切需要 " 健全和多模式 " 翻译。 这意味着同时管理多种通信流——将口头讲故事、活泼的插图、书面文字和数字媒体结合起来。 Kimbi说 : “ 我们不只用文字沟通, 我们不能再严格地认为翻译是一本书, 这种数字演变自然地与人工智能的兴起相交. 虽然代表们承认大赦国际在提高翻译速度、优化效率和降低少数民族语言的业务费用方面具有巨大潜力,但与会者保持战略谨慎的立场。 语言技术顾问Etienne Ondoa说, “技术加速了圣经翻译和语言发展的进步, 因此,他说,工作人员的能力建设仍然是最大的投资。 随着技术的发展,部内支持技术所需的技能也随之而来. Ondoa说,“技术领导在战略决策进程中应有发言权。 “技术决定日益影响部委的成果、健全的财政资源管理、网络安全、人工智能的采用和组织复原力。” Etienne Ondoa是全球教会的交响乐团, 它们的存在是为了为教会服务,而教会仍然是上帝执行全球任务的主要工具。 金比把运动的未来比作一个宏伟的全球安排. 他说,“现代圣经译本的特殊性在于它是一个多样化的合唱团——由各种影响组成的管弦乐团,为每个语言群体解释一首名为 " 脚本 " 的宏伟交响乐。 “在这个管弦乐团中,我们需要每个人:地方教会、口头宣传者、媒体创造者、扫盲专家和技术伙伴。” 故事:吕恩·普鲁登斯·姆冯多和艾萨克·福奇相片:艾萨克·福奇相片

title: God’s mission in Africa: ‘There is still much to do’
summary: For both the African and global audiences at the Yaoundé gathering, panel members underscored a fundamental truth: Bible translation is not an isolated academic exercise.
summary_zh: 在雅温得会议上，小组成员向非洲和全球观众强调了一个基本事实：圣经翻译并不是一项孤立的学术活动。
title_zh: 神在非洲的使命： “还有很多事情要做”
content: YAOUNDÉ, CAMEROON — During the Wycliffe Global Alliance Africa Area Gathering, a question was put before delegates: Is the African Church awake? A three-person panel, moderated by Dr. Zac Manyim, Director of the Department of Church and Scripture Engagement at CABTAL (Cameroon Association for Bible Translation and Literacy), delved into the continent’s strategic mission challenges and local breakthroughs. A Call from the Pulpit to Action ‘Yes, the African Church is awake, but it is not active,’ said Rev. Abel Chebe Ngah of the Apostolic Church in Cameroon. He noted a disparity in how modern ministry resources are being spent. ‘Some churches are focused on building megachurches, while only a few are focused on spreading the Word of God. The African church should have been doing exploits, but it is not yet doing so. There are still many areas in Africa not reached by the gospel.’ For the landscape to shift, Ngah argued that mission cannot be treated lightly; the local church must intentionally send missionaries. Demonstrating local ownership, his own denomination dedicates a specific Sunday every year entirely to Bible translation, using it to mobilise believers and raise financial support for CABTAL’s fieldwork. Though some local churches might lack the required financial resources, they offer abundant human and material resources needed in Bible translation. The Lifelong Impact of Mother-Tongue Literacy Pastor Alphonse Gamaldak, president of the Mofu Gudur Inter-Church Committee, said Bible translation reshaped his entire life trajectory. Before receiving any formal education, he learned to read and write in his mother tongue. This linguistic foundation gave him the leeway to master French, eventually leading him to seminary. ‘Yes, the church is awake in Mofu Gudur (a language community of northern Cameroon) because many kids have now grown and seen their lives transformed by the Bible translated into our language,’ he said. The impact extends far beyond the sanctuary. Through mother-tongue functional literacy programmes overseen by the translation project, community members have developed income-generating activities, drastically improving local livelihoods. Today, over 250 literacy teachers are actively instructing inside churches and surrounding villages. Yet, Pastor Gamaldak warned that sustainability requires ongoing investment. ‘There is still much to do,’ he said, ‘like continuing to build the capacity of and support these 250 literacy teachers.’ In 2008, when the Mofu Gudur New Testament was dedicated, the church and the community came together to facilitate the distribution. Five thousand copies were printed, and they were all sold out in the following months. A second run of 4,000 copies was printed. A few years later, it was still hard to obtain a copy. This motivated CABTAL to begin work on the Old Testament, which was dedicated in May 2026. Thanks to the commitment of the local church, the Mofu Gudur people now have a complete Bible. The Takeaway for the Global Alliance For both the African and global audiences at the Yaoundé gathering, panel members underscored a fundamental truth: Bible translation is not an isolated academic exercise. When local churches move from being merely ‘awake’ to being actively engaged, Scripture access unlocks deep spiritual maturity, local resource mobilisation and holistic community development. Story and Photos: Isaac Forchie
content_zh: 在威克里夫全球联盟非洲地区集会期间,向代表们提出了一个问题: 非洲教会醒了吗? 一个三人小组,由CABTAL(喀麦隆圣经翻译和识字协会)教会和圣经参与部主任Zac Manyim博士主持,探讨了非洲大陆的战略任务挑战和地方突破。 喀麦隆使徒教会的Abel Chebe Ngah牧师说, 他指出,在现代部委资源如何使用方面存在差距。 :"有些教堂专注于建造特大教堂,而只有少数教堂专注于传播"上帝之道". 非洲教会本应在进行剥削,但尚未这样做。 非洲仍有许多地区没有获得福音。 为了改变地貌,Ngarh认为不能轻视任务;当地教会必须故意派遣传教士. 他自己的教派每年专门用一个礼拜天翻译圣经, 尽管一些地方教会可能缺乏所需的财政资源,但它们提供了圣经翻译所需的大量人力和物力资源。 Mofu Gudur教会间委员会主席Alphonse Gamaldak教授的《母亲-通格识字牧师终身影响》说,《圣经》翻译重塑了他的整个人生轨迹。 在接受任何正规教育之前,他学会用母语读写. 这个语言学基础给了他掌握法语的回旋余地,最终引导他进入神学院. 他说 : “ 是的, 教堂在Mofu Gudur(喀麦隆北部的一个语言社区)醒了, 因为许多孩子已经长大, 影响远远超出避难所。 通过翻译项目监督的母语实用识字方案,社区成员开展了创收活动,大大改善了当地生计。 今天,250多名扫盲教师正在教会内部和周围的村庄积极进行教学。 然而,Gamaldak牧师警告说,可持续性需要持续投资。 他说,“还有许多事情要做,就像继续建设和支持这250名扫盲教师的能力。” 2008年,当"莫福古都尔新约"被奉献时,教会与社区聚集一堂来为发行提供便利. 印出五千本,后数月全部被卖出. 第二次印制了4000册. 几年后,仍难以获得副本. 这激励了CABTAL开始"旧约"的工作,该"旧约"于2026年5月被专门化. 由于当地教会的承诺,莫福古都尔人现在有了完整的"圣经". 小组成员强调了一个基本真理:圣经翻译不是孤立的学术活动。 当当地教会从仅仅是`觉醒'走向积极参与时,《圣经》的获取将释放出深刻的精神成熟、地方资源动员和整体社区发展。 故事与相片:以撒·福奇

content: Tuesday is the day most Christian publishers release their new books, so each week I let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. This week brings Andrew Walker’s diagnosis of our prodigal culture, a graphic-novel edition of The Pilgrim’s Progress , and Samuel James’s Scroll Less, Live More . On the academic side, you will find reference works and commentaries. You may also want to consider Trevin Wax’s liturgy for daily prayer. For each book, I’ve included the publisher’s description and its list of endorsers. Books for Everyone Crossway Prodigal Culture A People in Ruins and the Way Back Home Andrew T. Walker Endorsed by: R. Albert Mohler Jr., Carl R. Trueman, Allie Beth Stuckey, Seth Dillon, and Kristen Waggoner Publisher’s description We have forgotten what it means to be human. American men and women are feeling the despair of a counterfeit culture, one where polarization has replaced conversation, pornography is chosen over true intimacy, and marriage and family are postponed indefinitely. The resulting isolation has forced us to confront the truth: individualism and worldly systems cannot take the place of God’s design for humanity. This scholarly yet accessible study examines the effects of secularism, nihilism, and barbarism on culture today, and explains why a biblical worldview is essential for human flourishing. Andrew T. Walker skillfully confronts 10 pressing issues—including loneliness, sexual confusion, anti-institutionalism, and identity. Affirming that shared norms grounded in creation order are the solution to social decline, he champions a return to biblical standards of freedom, human nature, and purpose. Walker compares Western culture to the prodigal son in Scripture—a culture that has squandered its inheritance and must now decide whether it will return to the Father or continue living in squalor. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Crossway Scroll Less, Live More 10 Healthy Tech Habits for Teens Samuel D. James Endorsed by: Paul David Tripp, Matt Smethurst, and Whitney Newby Publisher’s description Nearly every teenager carries a smartphone in their pocket. What was once an innocent tool, providing a quick escape and a promise of connection, has now become a world that holds us captive. Looking up from the tiny pixels and refraining from the incessant scrolling may be the rest that our souls need. Scroll Less, Live More offers teens and families 10 practical habits for navigating the world of technology from a Christian perspective. From the author of the Christian Book Award winner, Digital Liturgies, tech-realist Samuel James applies his ideas into action steps to help teenagers keep digital tools in their proper place. By addressing how technology affects our social interactions, sleep patterns, critical thinking, and much more, James helps readers see the wisdom in God’s perfect design and, as a result, resist the temptations prevalent in the smartphone age. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Zondervan Get to Work Seeing Your Daily Grind as God’s Good Gift Jonny Ardavanis Endorsed by: R. Kent Hughes, R. Albert Mohler, Jr., Allie Beth Stuckey, and Colby Parkinson Publisher’s description Learn to avoid both passivity and burnout by discovering God’s glorious design for work—and how to labor, rest, and steward your time in ways that glorify God and maximize your joy. The average person will spend 90,000 hours working—a staggering third of their life. For many, these hours feel like a necessary burden, something we have to do. But what if work isn’t a punishment to endure, but a privilege to embrace—a divine “get to” rather than a grim “got to”? In a time of contradictory messages about work, hurry, and rest, pastor and author Jonny Ardavanis dives into Scripture to help you see work as a divine calling, guiding you to partner with God and find profound meaning and purpose in your daily work, whether you’re a plumber, a CEO, or a stay-at-home mom. As America heads to the polls, Christian voters may benefit from reminding themselves of the truths in this article and praying the prayer it provides. “On May 17, 1776, John Witherspoon stepped into the pulpit at Princeton on a day of fasting the Continental Congress had appointed for all the colonies. War had already begun and independence was less than two months away. Witherspoon, a Presbyterian minister and soon-to-be signer of the Declaration of Independence, called the occasion a ‘day of solemn humiliation.’ Before he said a word about the conflict, he turned his hearers’ eyes to the sovereign providence of God. He closed with a prayer: ‘God grant that in America true religion and civil liberty may be inseparable, and that the unjust attempts to destroy the one, may in the issue tend to the support and establishment of both.'” Looksmaxxing: The Normalizing of Vanity. Jacob Crouch: “To say it plainly, Christians don’t looksmaxx. However much we may be into fitness or beauty, we reject looksmaxxing on three levels: our worth, our temporality, and our purpose. Our beauty is temporary; and all our beauty is for His glory. Our beauty does not determine our worth, because our value is fixed in Christ.” A Wretch Like Me. title_zh: 法律的美丽
content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Zondervan . This article is taken from The Jesus Bible , from Passion Publishing and Zondervan. The Lord called Joshua to be strong and courageous as Joshua replaced Moses as Israel’s leader and led the people into the promised land. This calling was based on his obedience and submission to the Word of God. As the Creator, God knows how life is meant to be lived and the way for people to experience life to the full ( Jn 10:10). The gift of the law was a gracious act of God to instruct his people in his ways. It was never intended to be a moralistic plan to earn God’s favor. Rather, the law was given to those who had already experienced God’s redeeming grace. In the law, God provided instructions for how his children can love him and other people. This law is not a collection of arbitrary dictates from a malevolent deity, but instead it is the wisdom of God distilled in human language. It is a path to joy and life — the way people were meant to live. The Bible continually portrays the law of God in this fashion. For example, in the longest psalm in the Bible, Psalm 119, the author says that he loves, treasures, delights in and longs for the law. It is a source of hope, peace, joy and direction. In Psalm 19, the psalmist says the law refreshes the soul, makes wise the simple, gives joy to the heart and gives light to the eyes (Ps 19:7 – 8). The law is a beautiful gift from a gracious God. Jesus testified to the lasting value of the law when he said that he did not come to abolish the law (Mt 5:17). Instead, Jesus amplified the law, explaining the transformation that should result as a proper response to his work. In his masterful Sermon on the Mount in Matthew 5 through 7, Jesus called people to a far greater standard of obedience than mere conformity to external regulations. Instead of simply condemning murder, Jesus unmasked the anger that fueled this act. Adultery is not the prime culprit, but lust rooted in the human heart is the real problem. Jesus methodically outlined the heart-level change that the law relied upon. Rather than rendering the law obsolete, Jesus showed that the law continued to provide an authoritative standard and guidance for God’s people. Now, because of the finished work of Christ, believers have hope that the price for their disobedience of the law has been paid and that they have God’s Spirit dwelling within them, providing them the power to live the life God intends. 作为造物主,上帝知道生命的本意,知道人们如何体验到生命的完全(Jn 10:10). 法律的天赋是上帝的恩惠行为,以指示他的人民如何行事. 这从来就没有打算成为赢得上帝恩惠的道德计划。 相反,法律是给予那些已经经历过上帝赎回恩惠的人的。

在法律中,上帝为他的孩子如何能爱他和其他人提供了指示. 这部法则并不是从邪恶的神灵中任意地指令的集合,而是用人类语言来提炼出上帝的智慧. 这是通往快乐和生活的道路——人们本该生活的方式。 圣经以这种方式不断地描绘出上帝的法则.

耶稣不是简单地谴责谋杀,而是揭发了激起这一行为的愤怒. 通奸不是罪魁祸首,但植根于人心的欲望才是真正的问题. 耶稣有条不紊地概述了法律所依赖的心脏层面的变化. 耶稣没有使法律过时,而是表明法律继续为上帝的人民提供权威的标准和指导.

title: Tips for Resolving Conflict in Marriage
summary: Conflict in marriage is inevitable, but resolving it well is a skill. Here are 6 practical tips that range from examining your own sin first to a 10 p.m. rule. See Also Danger Signs of an Unhealthy Dating Relationship The Beginner’s Guide to Conflict Resolution Free Stuff Fridays
summary_zh: 婚姻中的冲突是不可避免的，但妥善解决冲突是一项技能。这里有6个实用技巧，从先检查你自己的罪到晚上10点的规则。另请参阅不健康约会关系的危险迹象周五解决冲突的初学者指南免费内容
title_zh: 解决婚姻冲突的技巧
content: It is inevitable that lives lived in deep intimacy will generate conflict. We wish this weren’t so, but sadly, it is. Therefore, wise couples learn to anticipate conflict and learn to resolve it well. I was recently asked to provide some thoughts on conflict resolution, and thought I’d share what I came up with. Yet as I have sat with couples and tried to help them work through various issues, it has shocked me to find how many have never learned to settle conflict well. Many set habits and patterns in their early years that become hard to break or overcome. I have met with couples who have only ever tried to resolve conflict by raising their voices, and with others who have only ever tried to resolve it by going silent. I have met with some who have only ever relied on text messaging instead of speaking face to face, and with others who have long since given up and don’t even bother trying anymore. Much of this stems from their first years and their failure to get well grounded in conflict resolution. To that end, here are a few suggestions on resolving conflict well. First, borrowing from Robert Murray M’Cheyne, follow this pattern: For every one look at your spouse’s sin, take ten at your own. It’s easy enough to become an expert in the way your spouse sins against you, but it’s far more important to become an expert in the ways you sin against your spouse. It concerns me when I see someone who seems adamantly committed to his spouse’s holiness but seemingly not very interested in his own. Your first calling before the Lord is to deal with your own sin so you can put it to death and come alive to righteousness. Second, invite your spouse to identify your sin. Because of the sheer quantity of the time and intimacy you share, you will inevitably sin against your spouse more than you will sin against anyone else. Not only that, but married life lets your spouse see the kinds of sins that no one else will. Only he or she sees how you sin in the bedroom, for example, or when you’re running late and nobody else is around. What’s more, your spouse sees deeper into your soul than anyone else and, therefore, knows more about you. In a healthy marriage, if you are truly committed to holiness, it only makes sense that you will ask your spouse to speak into your life. It is wise to provide a safe setting to do this where you won’t be a baby or a bully, and won’t sulk or lash out. Set aside some time, tell your spouse that you’d like to hear what sins you are committing, then listen patiently and calmly, without showing anger or being defensive. Having done that, go away, think about it, pray about it, and don’t respond until a day later. This could be a great means of grace in your life. Third, identify times when you won’t try to resolve conflict. Aileen and I, for example, have a long-established 10 o’clock rule, which means we won’t try to fix anything after 10 p.m. We are well aware that Ephesians 4:26 says, “Do not let the sun go down on your anger,” but we have also learned that some issues simply cannot be neatly resolved by bedtime. (Married folk will know that some of the most common conflicts tend to happen between the time you get into bed together and the time you actually fall asleep.) The later the day gets, the more we tend to operate out of emotion rather than reason. And some things seem way worse in the evening when we’re tired than in the morning when we’re fresh. So if we haven’t worked it out by 10, we will call a halt, kiss one another, pray with one another, say something like “I love you and we are going to be all right,” and then go to sleep. Then we can try to work it out at a better time, when we are in a better frame of mind. And honestly, in the light of day, we often realize the situation wasn’t nearly as dire as we thought and that it can be covered by love (1 Peter 4:8). Fourth, invite others in when necessary. Sometimes the most helpful thing you can do in a time of conflict is invite some friends or so

然而,当我与夫妇们坐在一起,努力帮助他们解决各种问题时,我发现有多少人从未学会妥善解决冲突,这让我感到震惊。 许多人在早年就设定了难以打破或克服的习惯和模式.

我见过夫妇们,他们只试图通过提高声音来解决冲突,而其他人则只试图通过沉默来解决冲突。 我会见了一些只依靠短信而不是面对面发言的人,

其主要原因是他们最初的岁月和未能在解决冲突中扎根。 为此,我们提出一些关于妥善解决冲突的建议。 首先,向罗伯特·默里·姆谢恩借款,遵循这一模式: 每看一看配偶的罪孽,就自己拿十。

成为你配偶对你的罪过的专家是很容易的, 当我看到有人 似乎坚定致力于他的配偶的圣洁,

你第一次在主面前召唤是 处理你自己的罪过 这样你就可以把它死 并活到正义。 其次,请您的配偶 识别你的罪恶。 由于你所分享的时间和亲密关系,你不可避免地会对你的配偶犯下比对其他人犯下更严重的罪行。

不仅如此 婚姻生活让你的配偶看到 别人不会犯的罪 只有他或她看到你在卧室的罪过, 更何况,你的配偶比任何人都更深刻地看待你的灵魂,从而更了解你。

在一个健康的婚姻中,如果你真正致力于圣洁,那么你要求你的配偶在你的生活中说话就只有道理了. 最好提供安全的环境,

也不要发怒或防卫。 并且直到一天后才回应。 这可能是你生命中伟大的恩典手段. 第三,确定你何时不会试图解决冲突。

例如艾琳和我早就有十点的规则, 我们清楚地知道,以弗所4:26说,“不要让太阳落在你的愤怒上,”但我们也了解到,有些问题根本不能通过睡觉来彻底解决。

(结婚后人们会知道,一些最常见的冲突往往发生在你们上床睡觉的时间与实际入睡的时间之间. 一天越晚,我们就越倾向于出于情感而不是理性而行动. 有些事情在晚上比早上更糟糕,

因此,如果我们还没有在10点之前解决,我们将叫停,互相亲吻,相互祈祷,说出类似“我爱你,我们会没事的”的话,然后睡觉。 然后,我们可以尝试在更好的时间,当我们处于一个更好的思维框架时,解决它。

老实说,在白天,我们常常意识到,情况没有我们想象的那么糟糕,而且可以被爱所覆盖(1:彼得:8). 第四,在必要时邀请其他人参加。 有时候,在冲突时期,你能做的最有帮助的事 就是邀请一些朋友

content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a lot of great books to start a new month. If all goes according to schedule, the list will include works on apologetics, singing, Karl Marx and D.L. Moody, missionaries who were recently martyred in Haiti, and much more. Enjoy the bounty! Logos users will want to take a look at this month’s free and nearly-free books. You’ll also find some early Black Friday deals that include some commentaries at up to 80% off. It’s also worth browsing the monthly sales . Recommended Reading A Candy Shop Owner, a Customs Officer, and a Beloved Family. I like this illustration. “Anyone traveling to another country knows that customs officers don’t mess around. They might grill you about what you are bringing into the country, who you are visiting, where you are going, and what your intentions are in the country. I’ve been asked all of those questions. I’ve never felt warmly welcomed by a customs officer. Currently our daughter lives in Southern California. We look forward to those sweet times she can come home. When she arrives home for Christmas, will we grill her? ‘What are the purposes of your stay at our home?’ ‘Who do you plan to visit?’ ‘What are you bringing into our home?’ Certainly not! We will throw the door open, wrap her in our arms, and welcome her in. She is family!” Your Definition of Blessing Is Too Small. “How do we square the Bible’s unblushing promises of blessing for the faithful with its theology of suffering? Put another way, how does Psalm 128 fit with a passage like Psalm 88, where the faithful one seems utterly abandoned to the darkness? One way to answer this question succinctly is to realize that the Bible, first, expands the meaning of blessing in this life, and second, eternalizes it.” These are helpful categories when we consider a difficult topic. 5 Ways Retirees Can Serve the Church. I am not yet a retiree, but when the time comes, this article lists some of the ways I will want to serve my church. “‘Retirement at last! Now I can sleep as late as I want to. Now I get to do nothing all day.’ Such is a popular description of how retirement looks to many people. I know some who would even add, ‘Now I get to play golf every day.’ Obviously, this does not reflect the Christian perspective of someone who understands that his chief end is ‘to glorify God and enjoy Him forever.’ This is not to say that sleeping later and playing golf are anti-Christian. However, there are some significant ways that retirees can still serve the church.” You Can See Everything: On Masks, Performing, and Holiness. You have probably heard at least something about the new film You Can See Everything . Joseph Whitenton explains that the movie provokes the question of whether you can ever truly know someone, then says “I can’t help but feel a deep sense of dread. Is this really all we can say about our relationships to one another? That it might be impossible to really know someone? To even know ourselves? Are our lives just a string of performances? I can’t help but think about how a social media centered age might further contribute to this feeling of constantly performing, as Bo Burnham, another comedian/prophet has observed.” The Straightest Path to Happiness. Randy Alcorn: “In God’s world, happiness is found in discovering what’s truly in our self-interest: loving God and our neighbor. This profound, paradigm-shifting concept, understood correctly, makes the false dichotomy obvious in the question, ‘Should I serve others, or should I act in my own best interests?'” The Danger of ‘No Enemies to the Right’. Writing for The Daily Wire , Andrew Walker tells about the danger of the slogan “no enemies to the right.” “There remains asymmetrical warfare in the Left’s continued aggression toward conservatives. Biblical fidelity also requires impartial judgment — even when it goes against ‘our side.’ Brothers and sisters on the Right need to hear that. When conservati

content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: When God Acts in Power Wikipop Weather Photographer of the Year Bring on the Dawn Big Words Men Sing 1. When God Acts in Power No element of God’s character can be separated from any other. You or I may use the power available to us recklessly, imperfectly, or sinfully—we may act forcefully yet unwisely, or authoritatively yet with evil motives and immoral outcomes. We may act impulsively, on the basis of false information, or in ways that foster prejudice or injustice. In this way, power can be used to bring about great good or great harm. But God never acts in such a way that he diminishes any part of his character. Hence, when God acts in power, he invariably exercises that power in ways that are wise, holy, just, good, and true. I think Jen Wilkin says this well: “The truth of God’s limitless power would be absolutely terrifying were it not paired with the truth of His limitless goodness.” God’s power separated from his other attributes would mean there is nothing that would withhold or restrain him. Yet God’s power paired with his other attributes is tremendously comforting, for we know he will use his power only in ways that are ultimately for our good and his glory. 2. Wikipop Wikipop is a microsite that offers the answer to just one question: What Wikipedia page was everyone looking at yesterday? You probably won’t be shocked to know that on Saturday, when I finalized this article, it told me that everyone had been looking for Patrick Stewart, who died a few days prior. (Note: I add this site with a bit of trepidation because I can’t predict what article will be featured on the day you click the link, so hopefully it’s nothing bad!) 3. Weather Photographer of the Year I know I keep sharing photography contests, but as I said last week, this is the time of year when many of them announce the winners. But this one is different from others I have shared since it features weather. In the Weather Photographer of the Year shortlist, you’ll find exactly what you’d expect—a stunning collection of photos of the weather. 4. Bring on the Dawn I know many people who have appreciated Douglas McKelvey’s Every Moment Holy books, which offer liturgies and prayers for all of life’s moments. Anchor Hymns recently collaborated with McKelvey on an album titled Bring on the Dawn that was inspired by his books. I’m pretty sure that if you appreciate the books, you’ll also like the music. 5. Big Words Sometimes the best apps are the simplest—the ones that do just one thing, but do it well. That’s the case with Big Words . What does it do? It lets you use your phone (or iPad or other screen) to display big words. “Make a full-screen sign, timer or message from a link. Hold up your phone at arrivals, put a countdown on the TV, or show the Wi-Fi password at the front desk. No account, no app, nothing stored on a server. The link is the whole display, so you can share it or bookmark it.” There is nothing to download, so you can just go ahead and bookmark it to use when the need arises. 6. Men Sing I love this delightfully countercultural “Men Sing” trend that’s happening among Dutch Reformed churches, and would love to see it spread. What is it? It’s just men getting together to sing hymns. I had hoped to attend the recent one in Hamilton, but was on the road at the time. Hopefully I can make it to the next one. You can find videos from churches in Hamilton , Grand Rapids , and Chilliwack . I assume it’s happening in other places where there are lots of Dutch Reformed churches. Well done, Dutch guys! 你或我可能会莽撞地、不完美地、或罪恶地使用我们所拥有的权力——我们可能会以邪恶的动机和不道德的结果,采取强而不明智或权威的行动。 我们可能根据虚假信息或以助长偏见或不公正的方式采取冲动行动。 这样,权力可以用来带来巨大的好坏.
但上帝从不以这样的方式行事,以致于削弱他性格的任何部分. 因此,当上帝行使权力时,他总是以明智、神圣、公正、善良和真实的方式行使这种权力。
我认为Jen Wilkin说得好 : “ 如果上帝无限力量的真理不与他无限善良的真理相配的话,那将是绝对可怕的。 ” 神的力量与他的其他属性相分离,将意味着没有任何东西可以扣留或约束他.
然而,上帝的力量与他的其他属性相配,是极为安慰的,因为我们知道,他只会以最终有利于我们及其光荣的方式使用他的力量。 2. Wikipop Wikipop是一个微站点,只回答一个问题:昨天大家看的维基百科页面是什么?

content: Good morning. My gratitude goes to Ligonier Ministries for sponsoring the blog this week to ensure you know about the new Grow app . It’s a free download and offers a lot of great content. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a variety of deals spanning a bunch of different eras and genres. Recommended Reading Jessica Lee writes about the growing no contact movement in which people sever their relationships with people they find toxic or problematic. I think of the young women I mentor who are flooded with reels, encouraging them that the best way to deal with the strained relationship with their mom is to put up higher boundaries that limit contact, or to cut off contact altogether. Even if they don’t take these drastic measures, they cannot help being influenced by the ideas, and neither can we. We are steeped in a therapy culture that talks a lot more about self-care than self-sacrifice, and we would be naive if we didn’t acknowledge the formative influence it has on us. And so, when relationships (whether with a parent, sibling, or friend) get hard, as they inevitably will, our first impulse is often toward self-preservation (putting up higher boundaries) and not self-sacrificial presence and faithfulness. Read: Going No Contact?: Ruth and Faithful Presence. Madeline Livingston has been going through a time of deep sorrow, and from that perspective writes a meditation about grief and glory. In my grief, I can turn to a Savior who has known human frailty and deep suffering, a Savior who in his most desperate moment prayed, “Let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will” ( Matthew 26:39 ). I can trust in the goodness and provision of a Father who did spare his own Son, but gave him up to rescue us and make us his own ( Romans 8:32 ). I can rest in the compassion of a Maker who collects all my tears in his bottle ( Psalm 56:8 ), a Good Shepherd who carries me safely through the lowest valley and restores my soul ( Psalm 23 ). As Sorrow and Suffering take me by the hand, they invite me to run to the solid ground of God’s promises made yes and amen through Christ. They urge me on to seek solace in the only place it can truly be found, in a arms of a Father who is my “refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble” ( Psalm 46:1 ). Read: When Sorrow & Suffering Take You by the Hand. Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra did a lot of interviews to try to arrive at some best practices for churches that are evangelistically effective. Her article offers a lot of food for thought. Thirty years ago, evangelical churches leaned on programs like Evangelism Explosion or Continuous Witness Training to deliver evangelistic focus and training, church leader Thom Rainer said. Those structured initiatives fit well in a culture that was more Christian and more institutionalized—it took an average of 20 church members to reach one person for Christ per year. Today, it takes 50, Rainer said. “Evangelism efficacy, evangelism effectiveness, has definitely diminished.” That trend is likely to continue. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. Read: Best Practices from Evangelistically Effective Churches. Like Darryl Dash, I’ve been hearing and reading a lot of doom and gloom lately, much of it related to the rise of AI. But also like Darryl, I don’t feel particularly alarmed. I read quite a few predictions of doom over the weekend, including some from self-professed tech optimists. Supposedly, some infrastructure in the United States is under attack. The idea is that AI is becoming too powerful and will overwhelm whatever safeguards we have in place to protect things like our water systems and electricity. The proposed solution is to prepare for the disaster by buying generators, solar panels for generators, and stockpiling water and other basic supplies. content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 感谢利戈尼耶各部赞助本周的博客, 这是免费的下载, 今天的销售和交易包括一系列跨越不同时代和流派的交易。 建议阅读 Jessica Lee写道,人们与他们发现有毒或有问题的人们断绝关系,但这种接触运动却在不断增加。 我想到那些我辅导的年轻女性,她们被卷轴淹没,鼓励她们,处理与母亲的紧张关系的最佳方式是设置更高的界限限制接触,或者完全切断接触. 即使他们不采取这些激烈的措施,他们也受不了这些想法的影响,我们也不能这样做。 我们身处一种治疗文化中,谈论自我护理比自我牺牲要多得多,如果我们不承认它对我们的形成影响,我们就会天真。 因此,当关系(无论是与父母、兄弟还是朋友的关系)变得困难时,我们的第一个冲动是往往朝向自我保护(提出更高的界限),而不是自我神圣的存在和忠诚。 读:去去不接触? 鲁斯和忠实的存在。 马德琳·利文斯通经历了一段深深的悲痛时期,从这个角度看,他写了一篇关于悲痛和荣耀的冥想. 在我悲痛中,我可以求助于一个知道人类脆弱和深重苦难的救世主,一个在他最绝望的时刻祈祷的救世主,“让这个杯子从我身边流过。 然而,不是我愿意,而是你愿意”(Matthew 26:39.). 我可以相信一个父亲的善良和供养,他确实饶了自己的儿子,但为了拯救我们而放弃了他,使我们成为自己的父亲(罗马8:32. 我可以安心地忍受一个造物主的怜悯,他把所有的眼泪都收在他的瓶中(诗篇56:8),一个好牧人,他把我安全地带入最底层的山谷并恢复我的灵魂(诗篇23. 当悲伤和受苦将我牵上手时,他们邀请我跑到上帝通过基督许下的承诺的坚实地步。 他们敦促我在一个真正能找到的地方寻求安慰,在一个父亲的怀抱中,他是我的“抵抗和力量,在困难中非常现成的帮助”(第46:1段)。 读取:"悲伤"和"受苦受难"由"手取""你"时. Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra做了很多访谈,试图为福音派有效的教堂达成一些最佳做法. 她的文章为思考提供了很多食物. 教会领袖汤姆·赖纳(Thom Rainer)说, 这些结构化的倡议非常适合一种更加基督教化和更加制度化的文化——平均每年需要20名教会成员为基督而接触一个人。 今天,它需要50,雷纳说。 “福音会的功效,福音会的功效,肯定已经下降。” 这一趋势很可能继续下去。 由于社交媒体和AI填补了我们的时间并增加了我们的社会焦虑,甚至连关系福音派也越来越困难. 读取:Evangelistic 有效教会的最佳做法。 与达里尔·达什(Darryl Dash)一样, 我最近也听到并阅读了许多末日与忧郁, 但与达里尔一样, 我读到很多关于周末末日的预言, 包括一些自以为是的技术乐观主义者的预言。 假设美国的一些基础设施受到攻击。 这个想法是AI正在变得太强大,并且会压倒我们现有的保护诸如我们的供水系统和电力之类的东西的保障措施. 拟议的解决办法是通过购买发电机、发电机太阳能电池板以及储存水和其他基本用品来为灾难做好准备。 然而,作者们承认,我们无法真正保护自己,使其免受歧视。

content: October was a strong month for new Christian books. I tried to keep you in the loop week by week, but I also wanted to provide a roundup for the end of the month. Of all the books that came our way in October, here are the ones that most stood out to me, arranged in what I think is a nice new format. As always, I’ve included the publisher’s editorial description for each. Book of the Month Crossway · Hardcover · 736 pages The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith If I had to put one book on the top of the stack this month, it would probably be this commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith—and I say that as a Baptist who respects, but does not hold to, the WCF. The contributors include Sinclair Ferguson, Chad Van Dixhoorn, and Kevin DeYoung. This is a reference work that pastors and serious readers will want to add to their libraries. “This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books For Your Own Soul Books for any thoughtful Christian reader. Crossway · Hardcover · 264 pages Finally Home: The Christian Hope of Heaven Dane Ortlund In this book, Dane Ortlund ( Gentle and Lowly ) turns his attention to heaven. He draws on Scripture, of course, and also on writers like Thomas Goodwin, Jonathan Edwards, and C. S. Lewis. “If we are not in Christ, this life is the best we will ever experience. If we are in Christ, this life is the worst we will ever experience. … In Finally Home , Dane Ortlund plunges into the word of God and the wisdom of the saints to help us rightly think about heaven, and to draw strength from our coming future more deeply than we ever have before.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books IVP · Paperback · 192 pages Everyday Discipleship: How Faith Shapes the Most Practical Areas of Life Jeremy Treat This is a practical book that teaches how following Jesus extends into every part of life, including those that are very ordinary, like meals, work, rest, and technology. It includes a discussion guide for groups. “Pastor Jeremy Treat understands this disconnect. In Everyday Discipleship , he dismantles the harmful sacred-secular divide that leaves many Christians feeling spiritually compartmentalized, uncertain about how faith applies to ordinary life, and unable to fully enjoy Christ in the entirety of our lives.” Buy it at Amazon Banner of Truth · Clothbound · 248 pages God Is Our Refuge and Strength: 150 Devotionals Through the Psalms William Boekestein & Rob Ventura Every Banner of Truth release is noteworthy, isn’t it? This one offers a short devotional reading to accompany each of the 150 psalms. “You need the Psalms. The Psalms are the Bible’s devotional heart. … Through brief, practical expositions of all 150 psalms, this volume proclaims, explains, and applies each one in light of the New Testament and the finished work of Jesus Christ the Lord.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books Counseling & Care Resources to care for Christians. One Measure Ministries · Redemption Press · Paperback workbooks SoulCare Groups™ Workbooks: Anxiety, Grief, and Sexual Integrity Gary & Linda Baer I am excited about the SoulCare Groups™ workbooks, which came out this month. Each is a twelve-week group study meant to be used alongside a few trusted biblical counseling books. The first three volumes cover anxiety, grief, and sexual integrity. “SoulCare Groups™, a biblical counseling workbook series from One Measure Ministries, equips churches to offer groups-based care through structured twelve-week topical studies.” Buy them at Amazon: Anxiety · Grief · Sexual Integrity For the Church and Its History Books to u
content_zh: 十月是基督教新书的强月. 我试图让你每周循环, 但我也想提供 一个回合的月底。 在10月我们走过来的所有书中, 这里有那些最突出的, 以我认为一种很好的新格式排列。 我总是把出版商的编辑描述都包括进去。 " 月之十字路口"一书 硬封面 736页 " 威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔:对其历史、神学和应用的综合评论 " 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑 如果这个月我不得不把一本书放在堆起的顶上,那很可能就是关于威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔书的评论——我说,作为一个尊重但不坚持周转基金的浸信会信徒。 撰稿人包括辛克莱·弗格森(Sinclair Ferguson),乍得·范迪克斯霍恩(Chad Van Dixhoorn)和凯文·德杨(Kevin DeYoung). 这是牧师和认真的读者想要加入他们的图书馆的参考作品. “这一系列重要的散文为21世纪的读者提供了一本《威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔指南》。 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其适用以及任何争议。” 在亚马逊购买, Crossway-Hardcover-264页 最后回家:天堂的基督教希望-丹麦奥特伦德 在这本书中,达尼·奥特伦德(英语:Dane Ortlund (Gentle and Lowly))将注意力转向了天堂. 他当然借鉴了"圣经",同时也借鉴了托马斯·古德温,乔纳森·爱德华兹和C·S·刘易斯等作家. “如果我们不是在基督中,这种生活是我们所经历的最好生活。 如果我们在基督, 这样的生活是我们所经历的最糟糕的。 . . . . . . . 最后,Dane Ortlund在“家园”中投入了上帝的言行和圣徒的智慧,帮助我们正确思考天堂,并比以往更深刻地汲取我们未来的力量。” 在亚马逊购买它 威斯敏斯特书 IVP 页面存档备份,存于互联网档案馆 192页 每日论文:信仰如何塑造最实用的生活领域 Jeremy对待 这是一本实用的书,教人们如何追随耶稣,如何延伸至生活的每一部分,包括那些非常平凡的,比如吃饭,工作,休息,以及技术等. 它包括为各团体编写的讨论指南。 “牧师Jeremy Treat理解这种脱节。 在日常的分歧中,他拆除了有害的神圣-世俗鸿沟,这些鸿沟使许多基督徒感到精神上的分化,对信仰如何适用于平凡的生活并不确定,无法在我们的一生中充分享有基督。” 248页《上帝是我们的庇护与力量》:150个通过诗人威廉·博克斯坦(William Boekestein)和罗布·文图拉(Rob Ventura)发行的《真理之行》值得注意, 这张是随150个诗歌的每个诗篇的简短的奉献读物。 “你需要诗歌。 圣诗是圣经的奉献之心。 . . . . . . . 通过对所有150个诗作的简短、实用的阐述,本卷根据《新约》和耶穌基督所完成的工作,宣布、解释和适用每个诗句。” 在Amazon 公司购买, 我对本月推出的“SoulCare Groups”工作手册感到兴奋。 每项研究都是为期12周的团体研究,目的是与一些值得信赖的圣经辅导书籍一起使用。 前三卷收录了焦虑,悲伤和性完整性. “SoulCare GroupsTM是《一个计量部》的一本圣经咨询工作手册系列,它使教会有能力通过结构化的12周专题研究提供基于群体的护理。” 在亚马逊购买:焦虑 · 悲伤 · 教会及其历史书籍的性正直

content: Good morning. I am making my way home from Colorado today after a productive series of meetings and video shoots. I’ll look forward to a more normal week next week! In the meantime, be sure to check in tomorrow for Weekend A La Carte and on Sunday for a favorite feature, Works & Wonders. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of interesting books like an exposition of the London Baptist Confession, some brief biographies of Christians you should know, and Thaddeus Williams’s book on reverence. Some of my books are 50% off at ChurchSource in their print editions: Visual Theology , A Visual Theology Guide to the Bible , and Pilgrim Prayers . Recommended Reading Time Flies—and Death Comes Speedily. The older you get, the more you come to understand that time flies and death comes speedily. “As teenagers, my friends and I were awash with youthful pride, poking fun at weighty things we knew little about—completely ignorant that our life here below is ‘a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes.’ The dew was still afresh upon our heads; the road of life unfurling in a great spool before our feet, disappearing into the far-off horizon. We could quote you verses here and there from the Scriptures, all the while being completely unversed in this point: “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for this is the end of all mankind, and the living will lay it to heart.” In our minds, we could afford to mock death because we were, at the time, so far removed from it.” Was Piper Unprepared? A little while ago, John Piper indicated that he may have been unprepared for pastoral ministry when he began it. In this episode of Ask Pastor John , he is asked to explain what he meant by that. Take Your Faith Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. During a time of spiritual decline, God used the Protestant Reformation to bring renewal to His church through the recovery of the biblical gospel. This Reformation Day, explore the truths that fueled renewed devotion to God and His Word in the Grow app from Ligonier. Discover hundreds of Reformation-themed articles, video teaching series, and conference messages to help strengthen your faith and deepen your walk with Christ. Download the Grow app today. (Sponsored) The Engineering Behind Every Heartbeat. This is a celebration of the engineering of the human heart. “The human heart does not beat like a perfect clock. The time between beats changes as the body breathes, moves, rests, and reacts to the world around it. New research shows that these changes are part of a feedback system linking the heart, brain, and nerves. The heart keeps a steady rhythm while remaining flexible when needed, much like a well-built control system.” When You Trick-or-Treat, Nod to Martin Luther. Daniel Hyde writes in a local paper to explain to its readers the Protestant contribution to Halloween. “So, by all means, dress up and hand out the candy. When the doorbell rings, remember: The principle that no authority may command conscience protects the civil liberty of the religious and nonreligious alike.” God’s Left Hand. Bryce Waller: “The most difficult part about politics is what happens after the elections. In Romans 13:1, God calls us to be subject to these governing authorities—to obey the laws they pass, to show them honor and respect, to give them our hard-earned money by paying taxes. Voting is one thing, but submitting my life to a politician, showing respect to that guy , paying taxes to those people —even the people I didn’t choose? That’s not so easy.” These are good things to work out before an election since it will shape your response, whether you are happy with the results or dismayed. 17 Exhortations For Christian Citizens. On a somewhat related note, here are 17 exhortations for Christian citizens. “Bad government and national decline grieve those who love their country and bring a kind of chaos—a hard providence for Christian citizens. Yet even worse form
content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 今天我从科罗拉多州回家的路 经过一系列富有成效的会议和录像拍摄。 我期待下周能更正常一点! 同时,请务必在明天的周末A La Carte 和星期日的首选节目Works & Wonders 登入。 今天的销售与交易交易包括许多有趣的书籍,如伦敦浸信会忏悔书的展出、一些你应该知道的基督教徒的简略传记以及Thaddeus Williams的"敬重"一书。 我的一些书在Church Source的印刷版中, 被推荐阅读"时空飞翔"——死亡会迅速来袭. 越老越了解时间飞逝 " 少年时,我的朋友和我充满了青春的自豪感,对我们所知甚少的重量级事物玩得很开心——完全不知道我们下面的生活是`一段短暂出现的雾,然后消失'。 露水仍然浮出水面;生命之道在我们脚前的大水池中被冲出,消失在遥远的地平线上。 我们可以在此地和那部经典中引用你们的迹象,当时,他们对于这部经典是毫无知识的。你们去哀号之所胜过去宴会之所胜过去宴会之所胜;这是全人类的结局,是活人的心事。 在我们心目中,我们可以以死亡为笑柄,因为我们当时远离死亡。” Piper没有准备好吗? 不久之前,约翰·皮珀表示他开始牧业时可能还没有准备好. 在"问约翰牧师"这集里 他被要求解释他的意思 在精神衰落的时期,上帝利用了新教的改造,通过恢复圣经福音给他的教堂带来复兴。 在利戈尼耶的"成长的应用"中,探索那些促使人们重新忠于上帝和他的话的真理。 发掘出上百篇以改革为主题的文章,视频教学系列,以及会话等信息来帮助增强你的信仰并深化与基督的行走. 今天下载 Grow 应用程序 。 (赞助)"每个心跳"背后的工程. 这是对人类心脏工程的庆祝. “人的心不像一个完美的钟。 随着身体的呼吸、移动、休息和对周围世界的反应,间隔时间会改变。 新的研究表明这些变化是连接心脏,大脑和神经的反馈系统的一部分. 心脏保持平稳的节奏,同时在必要时保持灵活,就像一个完善的控制系统。” 当Trick -or -Treat, 点头马丁路德。 丹尼尔·海德在当地的一篇文章中向读者解释新教对万圣节的贡献. “所以,无论如何,要穿好衣服,把糖果递出去。 当门铃响起,记住: 任何当局不得控制良心的原则保护宗教和非宗教的公民自由。” 上帝的"左手"。 布莱斯·沃勒(Bryce Waller):"政治方面最困难的部分是选举之后发生的事情. 在罗马13:1中,上帝号召我们服从这些执政当局——服从他们通过的法律,向他们表示荣誉和尊重,通过交税来给他们我们辛苦得到的钱. 投票是一回事,但把我的生命交给一位政治家, 对他表示尊敬, 这并非易事。 这些是选举前要解决的好事情,因为它将决定你的反应,无论你对结果满意还是沮丧。 17 对基督教公民的劝告。 与此相关的是,对基督教公民提出了17条劝告。 “坏政府和民族衰落使那些热爱祖国并带来某种混乱的人感到悲痛——这是基督教公民的难能可贵。 更糟糕的形态

content: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include books about the Old Testament, Proverbs, faithful presence, the life and influence of Tim Keller, and a whole lot more. Westminster Books is continuing their Reformation sale by offering discounts on ESV Bibles as well as the tremendous new 500th anniversary edition of Tyndale’s New Testament. Recommended Reading How the Mainstream Recruits for the Manosphere. Aaron Renn explains how “asymmetric blame, hectoring lectures, and selectively revived norms are driving young men to the influencers the mainstream condemns.” How Mental Illness Became an Identity. Myles Werntz has an interesting review of a new book by Fredrik deBoer that explains how mental illness became an identity. “Mental illness in the 21st century is an expanding category—and one increasingly dominated by its most functional and therefore visible members. That displacement—in our collective imagination and public discourse—of the profoundly mentally ill by my college students didn’t happen all at once. And how did it happen? Was it because of the closure of traditional mental hospitals, like those of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest ? Was it because of the internet-driven phenomenon of self-diagnosis by very functional influencers? The marginalization of psychiatry as a profession? Or denial, romanticization, and politics?” It Can Happen Here, Too. “As numerous countries in Europe experience riots, many in America are asking, ‘What on earth is happening on the continent that was, in many ways, the cradle of Western civilization?’ As historic buildings, places of worship, and commercial properties combust before our eyes on the nightly news, how are we to make sense of this?” Carl Trueman warns that what’s happening in Europe could also happen in the United States. 8 Ways to Help Your Kids Love the Church. Shiphrah Lakka offers a series of ways to help your kids learn to love the church. “While discipleship at home is extremely important and something every Christian parent should pursue, it can never replace the church. Reading Scripture together, praying as a family, and teaching our children about God within our homes are vital practices. Yet God’s design for believers extends beyond the walls of our homes. He calls us to belong to a community of believers who worship, serve, and do life together.” I Hate Your Halloween Decorations. Marc Sims writes about the reality of Halloween today. “The next time I am out, we will really slow down to take in the diorama you set up of black hooded figures encircling a pentagram-alter with a fake infant set in the middle of it, that way he can become familiar with Satanic rituals and child sacrifice. I mean, where else is he going to get this important cultural experience? Apparently, you are under the impression that becoming desensitized to violence and death is an important step for our whole neighborhood to take in—to celebrate, even. Here, frumpy old Marc ( boooo! ) was worried about why our culture seems ever more eager to relish death and the demonic—but you have shown me that this is really just fun! Save a fake a corpse for me!” Why Paper Books Endure. Daniel Darling explains his ongoing love for paper books (even while he’s not entirely opposed to electronic ones). “When I began my writing career in the early 2,000s, every single writing conference I attended featured speakers who issued grave warnings. E-books would eventually take over. Paper books would be a thing of the past. Libraries are nice relics of another era. Except that didn’t happen.” Something Worth Doing These words by Maltbie Davenport Babcock have often been a challenge to me, and I wouldn’t be surprised if they challenge you as well. title: Is It a Sin to Use AI Porn?
summary: What happens when the people in porn are not real exist, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create ethical pornography that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with real pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn? See Also 10 Ugly Numbers Describing Pornography Use in 2017 10 Articles on Pornography 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now
summary_zh: 当色情片中的人并不真实存在，而只是由人工智能产生时，会发生什么？人工智能是否允许我们制作道德色情作品，以解决真实色情作品带来的首要问题之一？换句话说，看人工智能生成的色情片是一种罪恶吗？另请参阅2017年描述色情使用的10个丑陋数字10篇关于色情的文章7个现在停止观看色情的好理由
title_zh: 使用人工智能色情片是罪过吗？
content: Over the past two decades, I have written a great deal about pornography . At many different times and in many different forms, I have urged people to consider a long list of arguments against it. I’m thankful to have interacted with many people who have come to see pornography as evil and who have committed themselves to sexual purity. Some of the strongest and most effective arguments against using pornography are based upon the humanity of the people who are involved in it. So, for example, in “ 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now ,” I wrote that we need to consider the cost to those who make it. “Pornography exacts a high cost of those who create it—the cost to their bodies, to their souls, to their mental well-being, to their dignity, to their future. A vast amount of the pornography you enjoy is created by people against their wills. The simple fact is, by watching porn, you are watching rape and deriving pleasure from it. You become a willing participant in sexual violence and you allow that actor on the screen to suffer for your pleasure.” Even if some pornography is consensual, a great deal of pornography is not, and the viewer cannot know which is which. Similarly, in “ 8 Sins You Commit Whenever You Look at Porn ,” I said that those who watch it are guilty of sexual assault. “A person who drives a getaway car for a band of bank robbers will rightly be charged with murder for anyone who is killed in committing that crime. The person who voluntarily watches sexual assault for purposes of titillation is rightly guilty of that sexual assault. And a nauseating quantity of pornography is violent in nature, displaying men taking advantage of women. Sometimes these women have volunteered for such degradation and sometimes they are forced or raped into it. To watch such horrifying smut is to be a participant in it and to bear the moral blemish of it.” While these are far from the only arguments against pornography, I believe they are especially effective ones. But what happens when the characters involved in pornography are no longer people? What happens when they no longer exist at all, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create “ethical pornography” that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with “real” pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn ? (For our purposes, we will assume that we are already rejecting deepfake porn—using the likeness of an existing person—as morally repugnant and both immoral and illegal. Instead, we are considering images of people who are generated entirely by AI.) The simple answer is yes: it is as sinful to look at AI-generated porn as it is to look at human-created porn. While some of the arguments may not be as relevant, the majority are unchanged. Before I explain how and why, I want you to listen to a warning: we are all experts at circumventing the spirit of the law by abiding within the strict letter of the law. There is something deep within us that wants to defy the rules that are given to us, and we become skilled at justifying the ways we do this. Often this involves reducing morality to a strict binary, then convincing ourselves that because we have not blatantly broken the law, we have abided by it. This was exactly the sin of the Pharisees of Jesus’s day who would strictly tithe the spices they grew in their gardens, yet fail to live according to the higher principles of justice, mercy, and faithfulness. There is something of the Pharisee in each one of us. With that in mind, here are reasons why it is a sin to use pornography that has been generated by AI. You are still lusting , even if you are lusting after a person who exists only on a screen. To lust is to long for an illicit sexual pleasure, and to long for an illicit sexual pleasure is to find satisfaction in what God has forbidden. content_zh: 在过去20年里,我写了很多关于色情的内容。 在许多不同的时刻,我以许多不同的形式敦促人们考虑一长串反对它的论点。 我很感激与许多人互动, 一些强烈而最有效的反对使用色情作品的论据是基于参与其中的人的人道. 因此,例如,在“停止看色情电影的7个好理由”中,我写道,我们需要考虑制作者的成本。 " 色情制品的制作者付出了高昂的代价 -- -- 他们的身体、灵魂、精神健康、尊严、未来的代价。 你所欣赏的大量色情作品都是由人们违背自己的意愿所创造的. 简单的事实是,通过看色情片, 你正在看强奸,并从中获得乐趣。 你成为性暴力的自愿参与者,你允许屏幕上那个演员为取悦而受苦。” 即使有些色情作品是合意的,但大量的色情作品却不是,观众也无法知道哪个是. 同样,在“每当你看到色情制品时,你就会犯下八起罪行”中,我说,观看色情制品的人犯有性侵犯罪。 “为一帮银行劫匪驾驶逃跑的汽车的人,将因犯下这种罪行而被杀害的人受到谋杀的指控。 自愿观看性攻击以达到抚慰目的的人理应犯有性攻击罪。 而令人恶心的色情作品数量在性质上是暴力的,展现出男性利用女性. 有时,这些妇女自愿从事这种有辱人格的工作,有时她们被迫或被强奸。 目睹这种令人发指的一团糟,就是参与其中,并承担其中的道德污点。” 虽然这些与反对色情制品的唯一论点相去甚远, 但是当参与色情的人物不再是人时会怎样呢? 当它们不再存在,而只是由AI产生时会发生什么? 大赦国际能否允许我们制造出“道德色情制品”,解决与“真正的”色情制品有关的最主要关切之一? 换句话说,看AI生成的色情片是不是罪过? (为了我们的目的,我们将假定,我们已经在拒绝利用像现有个人那样的深层假色情,认为这种色情在道德上是令人厌恶的,既不道德又非法。) 相反,我们正在考虑完全由大赦国际创造的人的形象。 ) 简单的回答是:看AI生成的色情片和看人造色情片一样罪恶. 虽然有些论点可能并不那么相关,但大多数论点没有改变。 在我解释方式和原因之前,我要你们聆听一个警告:我们都是通过遵守严格的法律条文来规避法律精神的专家。 我们内心深处有些东西想藐视赋予我们的规则,我们变得有技巧为我们这样做的方式辩护。 这往往涉及将道德降低为严格的二进制,然后说服自己,因为我们没有公然违法,我们遵守了法律。 这恰恰是耶稣时代的法利赛人的罪过,他们严格地说要将自己在花园所种的调味品的两倍之多,但却未能按照正义、慈悲和忠诚的更高原则活下来。 我们每个人都有法利赛人 考虑到这一点,以下是使用大赦国际制作的色情制品的罪责。 你仍然在贪欲, 即使你在贪欲 一个人只存在于屏幕上。 性欲是渴望非法的性快感,而渴望非法的性快感是寻求上帝所禁止的满足. 是为了让上帝之外的东西成为你欢乐的必备之物——在这种情况下,是性释放,而这种性释放会伴随着对一个...
